findings.title: No workflow-engine slice: workflow-as-data has no roadmap home
findings.visionNeed: v2's central engine (§2, implied capabilities): the development workflow is DATA the owner edits — add/reorder/extend steps, per-step tool bindings (agents, terminals, MCP tools), triggers (manual|event|schedule), and run history. The 24h prod-error loop, metrics→sprint planning, and custom chains are all instances of this one engine — v2 calls it the product's growth mechanism.
findings.gap: Overview §3 (S0–S8+Pv2) has zero workflow/scheduler/trigger/cron hits (grep-confirmed across overview, architecture.md, all specs; only CI 'workflows' in traceability.md:110). No slice owns WorkflowDefinition/WorkflowRun/StepState/Trigger; Kanban (S5) models task STATE, not process DEFINITION. Every v2 recurring capability is currently unbuildable AND undesignable — no slice can even declare a dependency on it. The map itself lacks the subsystem.
findings.recommendation: Add slices to overview §3 + dependency diagram: SW1 'Workflow engine core' — versioned WorkflowDefinition (ordered/DAG steps; step = {kind, tool-binding, params}; step kinds: agent-turn | terminal-command | mcp-tool | human-approval), WorkflowRun/StepState persistence in the core-owned store per the Data-layer charter, step executor, manual trigger; deps S3, Pv2, S6a. SW2 'Scheduler + event triggers' (see V8). SW3 'Workflow editor UI' (add/reorder/edit steps, bind tools, run-history view). Recurring actions, the self-healing loop, and metrics→sprint are then authored as definitions on top.
findings.connectsTo: V2 (execution home), V6 (S6b loop = default definition), V7 (ordering before S6b), V8 (scheduler), V9 (event bus), V10 (StepBinding/Tool Registry), V14 (charter storage rows), V32/V33 (reusable substrate); consumed by S6b/S6c/S5/S7/S8 and by V5's self-healing loop and V19's sprint planning.

findings.title: No process can host unattended/scheduled execution: agents + app-domain store are GUI-bound, daemon is charter-barred
findings.visionNeed: v2 north-star (c): 'hours agents progress unattended'; the 24h self-healing loop and metrics watching must fire whether or not the panel is open, survive restart, and never silently stop — 'the owner never polls'.
findings.gap: Three locked decisions jointly foreclose this: overview §4 puts app-native agents (CEO/PM/eng) 'in the core process' (the Tauri GUI app, dies on window close); the Data-layer charter puts S3+ domain data (hence future schedule/run state) in the core-owned store; and the charter bars bpa-sessiond — the ONLY always-on, launchd-supervised process — from becoming the app's general engine/database. Survival truth table: 'Agent runs (S6+) — undefined until S6b'. As architected, recurring workflows degrade to app-open-only — the exact attention tax v2 declares the enemy. The decision also determines WHERE the entire v2 entity store physically lives, so it must precede the S3 store-engine decision, not wait for S6.
findings.recommendation: Record a locked ADR in overview §2 BEFORE the S6b spec, choosing: (a) a second launchd-managed headless orchestrator process (e.g. bpa-orchd/bpa-workflowd) owning the app-domain store + scheduler + engine runtime, GUI attaching as a client — mirrors the proven sessiond pattern and reuses Pv2 §6 drain/consent upgrade choreography; (b) widen sessiond's charter with a strictly separated orchestration domain/DB (riskiest for the hardened daemon); or (c) honest v0 degradation: schedules fire only while the app runs, with catch-up-on-launch semantics, surfaced never silent — recorded as a conscious deferral. Either way add a 'workflow runs / agent runs' row to the canonical survival truth table.
findings.connectsTo: Gates V1 (SW2 scheduler host) and S6b agent-state survival; determines the physical home of every entity in V4/V5/V14/V19; Pv2 multi-subscriber attach already supports orchestrator+GUI co-attaching one session; interacts with BL-19 auto-updater, D4 upgrade choreography, and the launchd runbook.

findings.title: No MCP client subsystem: the product's stated extension mechanism has no delivery vehicle
findings.visionNeed: v2 §3 + implied capabilities: an MCP client INSIDE the product — connect/authorize/invoke external MCP servers (prowl.chat first) as tool providers for agents and workflow steps; 'the system grows by adding more tools… and by connecting MCP servers'; the flagship pipeline's research stage is literally an MCP call (idea → [research via prowl] → task).
findings.gap: Zero MCP mentions in overview/specs/backlog (grep: only the vision-v2 file). S6a is the LLM-PROVIDER layer (model calls: OpenRouter/OpenAI/GLM) — a different axis from MCP tool-providers. No slice covers server registry, transports (stdio + Streamable HTTP), JSON-RPC client, auth, tool discovery, typed invocation, or error/degradation. Without a named slice, the MCP client gets improvised mid-S6b under delivery pressure — the exact anti-pattern prior audit A8 fixed for the LLM layer — and the prowl research step cannot run at all.
findings.recommendation: Add roadmap row 'S-MCP / S6m — MCP client subsystem' parallel to S6a (deps: S3 core-owned store for the registry + BL-20 Keychain pattern; explicitly NOT Pv2 — MCP is core-process outbound JSON-RPC that never touches the Hop-B wire — and NOT S6a). Scope: server registry (add/enable/disable), authorization (API key / OAuth 2.1), tool discovery + tool-list-changed notifications, typed invoke with retries/timeouts/honest degradation, per-call cost/latency records (mirror S6a's capture rule), management UI. DoD: prowl.chat connected, tools listed, one research tool invoked with the result persisted as a durable artifact. Verify current MCP spec + SDKs via Context7 at spec time (fast-moving protocol). Document in §2/§4 that MCP tool-providers and LLM model-providers are two DIFFERENT abstractions.
findings.connectsTo: Powers V4's research stage and V5's research step; supplies V10's Tool Registry; credentials via V12; security posture via V13; session state via V27; surface bounding via V28; ordering via V29; S6b/S6e and V1's mcp-tool step kind are consumers.

findings.title: Idea entity + lifecycle missing: the mission's entry point has no data model
findings.visionNeed: v2 §1 + mission: 'take ANY idea to a working project' — Idea as a first-class entity: captured on the home screen, attached to an existing project OR spawning a NEW project, optionally sent to research (prowl MCP), flowing idea → [research] → task → subtasks → design → development with a tracked lifecycle (captured → researched → specced → in-dev → shipped).
findings.gap: No Idea entity anywhere: S3 models Projects+Goals/Context only; the Data-layer charter enumerates projects/goals/kanban/graph; overview §4 step 1 assumes goals already exist with no ingress for a raw idea; S5 columns are task-only. There is no idea→new-project bootstrap (the mission's core action, which must create Project+Workspace scaffolding), and Ideas sit UPSTREAM of Goals — bolting them on after S3 locks its schema and export/import contract forces a second S3-scale migration one slice later, and 'idea spawns project' constrains the Project model S3 is about to lock (project-less ideas or atomic auto-create).
findings.recommendation: Expand the S3 row to 'Projects + Goals + Ideas data model' and the charter entity list now: Idea (id, title, body, status lifecycle, project_id NULLABLE until it joins/spawns a project, timestamps) + provenance link slots to research artifacts, goals, and tasks it produces. Spec both ingress actions: 'add idea to project' and 'spawn project from idea' (consumes S3 Project⇄Workspace mapping + S2 workspace creation), each ≤2 actions. Make Idea an explicit CEO/S6 input (overview §4 step 1 gains 'or from a captured Idea'). Keep the idea→research→task PIPELINE out of S3 — it is a WorkflowDefinition (V1); only entity + CRUD land in S3.
findings.connectsTo: Head of the pipeline V1 orchestrates; research stage consumes V3 (prowl) and lands artifacts via V21; produces tasks per V22's provenance model; surfaces as quick-capture on V20's home screen; upstream of S3 Goals and S5 tasks.

findings.title: Per-project production error/log ingestion missing — the self-healing loop fails at its first input
findings.visionNeed: v2 §2 + implied capabilities: 'every 24h analyze the project's PRODUCTION error logs'; 'log/error ingestion per project' — the input data of the flagship loop 'the project watches its own production errors and fixes them'.
findings.gap: No ingestion concept exists. The system's only log-shaped data is TERMINAL scrollback from the dev machine; production telemetry is a different source entirely. S7 is INTERNAL app observability (LLM traces, agent spend/error rates — easily mis-read as covering this); S8 is future product-analytics integrations feeding the CEO. Grep for ingest/sentry/error-log/log-source across docs/specs = 0 hits. Missing wholesale: per-project error-source configuration (error-tracker APIs, hosting-provider log pulls, file tails, MCP-provided log tools), transports with retries + honest degradation, a normalized error-event schema with signature/dedup identity (prod errors repeat thousands of times), and a storage home. Every downstream loop step (triage, research, fix tasks, verification) is unbuildable without it.
findings.recommendation: Add roadmap row 'S9a — Project telemetry ingestion' (deps: S3 project entity; consumed by V1's engine): per-project error/log source registry (LogSourceConfig: source type, endpoint/path, credentials→Keychain, poll cadence), pull/tail/MCP transports with retries + honest degradation, normalized ErrorEvent records (fingerprint hash, count, first_seen/last_seen, sample payload — dedup by fingerprint so volume stays bounded), retention. Clearly distinguish from S7's app-internal observability in overview §3. Share one connector substrate with the reshaped S8 metrics ingestion (V19). Source credentials reuse BL-20's Keychain decision.
findings.connectsTo: Feeds V18 (study queue), V5-loop research via V3/V24, V23 (verification watches ingested events); event-triggers V8's scheduler; charter/retention home in V26; the composed self-healing loop is a scheduled WorkflowDefinition on V1+V2.

findings.title: Overview §4 hardcodes the orchestration loop as workflow-as-CODE, foreclosing owner-editable workflows
findings.visionNeed: v2 §2: 'The development workflow itself must be updatable by the owner: add steps, reorder, extend… custom chains, composable steps' — the CEO→PM→eng pipeline and its 'design' stages (brainstorm→spec→plan) are DATA the owner edits, not compiled agent logic.
findings.gap: Overview §4 (lines 132–142) specifies 'The orchestration loop (unchanged vision)' as a fixed five-step CEO→PM→specialists→workers→escalation pipeline; the S6b row scopes 'Agent runtime + ONE role end-to-end' as bespoke control flow. Nowhere is the loop described as a stored, editable definition. If S6b/S6c ship as scoped, the pipeline is compiled into the agent runtime and retrofitting editable steps means rewriting the runtime, run-persistence/resumability, and the escalation wiring — the locked-contract-forces-rework failure mode. 'Design' likewise stays baked into S6b code rather than being a reorderable pipeline stage.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite §4's loop preamble now: 'the CEO→PM→eng loop is the DEFAULT WorkflowDefinition — an instance of workflow-as-data executed by the engine (SW1); owners can edit, reorder, and extend it.' Re-scope S6b to run its role loop via the engine's step executor rather than bespoke control flow, and express 'design' (brainstorm→spec→plan) as named, reorderable steps when the engine lands.
findings.connectsTo: Depends on V1 (SW1) existing; enforced by V7's ordering; S6e custom agents become custom step/agent definitions on the same substrate; V22 carries the task/subtask side of the pipeline stage model.

findings.title: Slice order bakes in rework: workflow engine must land between S6a and S6b; S6c's inbox must be generic
findings.visionNeed: v2 needs the engine to exist BEFORE the agent pipeline hardens: the pipeline is a workflow instance, approval gates are a reusable step type ('policy-gated actions wait in ONE inbox'), and custom chains presuppose composable steps.
findings.gap: Current order S6a → S6b (hardcoded PM loop) → S6c (escalation inbox) → S6d/S6e, with no workflow slice in the graph — any future engine lands after S6e by default. Building runtime + escalation first bakes the pipeline into code (V6) and builds the approval inbox as agent-specific, when v2 needs approval-as-a-step reusable by ANY workflow (deploy consent in the 24h loop, spend gates). Rework of two slices is the cost of ordering alone. This is the v2-specific consequence of prior-audit A17 ('S6 hides 6+ subsystems'): the missing subsystem now has a MANDATORY position in the order.
findings.recommendation: Insert SW1 between S6a and S6b in the §3 table and diagram (S6b depends on SW1). Define S6c's inbox as the UI over a generic 'approval-gate step / escalation event' emitted by engine runs AND agent runs. SW2 (scheduler/events) and SW3 (editor UI) can follow S6c without blocking it.
findings.connectsTo: V1 (the slices being ordered), V6 (what the wrong order forecloses), V33 (S6c as the reusable gate), prior audit A17.

findings.title: Scheduler + trigger semantics missing: cron/event triggers, catch-up, overlap control, approval-suspend
findings.visionNeed: v2 §2 + implied capabilities: 'a scheduler (cron-like), event triggers' — the 24h prod-error cadence, metrics watching, and recurring sprint planning all hang off it; triggers are time-based AND event-based; runs must be observable.
findings.gap: Nothing in the roadmap runs anything on a schedule (grep schedul|cron|recurring|trigger = 0 relevant hits). S6b agent runs are user/CEO-initiated one-shots. Beyond mere existence, no doc names the production-grade semantics: persisted schedule definitions, missed-run/catch-up policy after host downtime, overlap control (don't start run N+1 while N is live), durable suspend/resume when an unattended run parks on an S6c approval (must wait in the inbox and resume on approve, surviving restarts), dedupe, and failure escalation. A naive timer that silently skips or double-fires is the default outcome.
findings.recommendation: Spec SW2 explicitly: trigger types cron | event (e.g. new-error-ingested, metric threshold) | manual on WorkflowDefinitions; missed-run catch-up policy; concurrency/overlap control; durable 'awaiting-approval' run state resumed by inbox action; alert-on-consecutive-failures routed to the S6c inbox; schedule fires and runs recorded in WorkflowRun history so the control panel can observe them. Host process per V2's ADR.
findings.connectsTo: Part of V1; host decided by V2; fires V5's loop and V19's sprint planning; suspend/resume binds to V33 (S6c); health surfaced via V25 (S7).

findings.title: No internal domain event bus — event triggers, live kanban moves, and the home feed will each invent eventing
findings.visionNeed: v2 event triggers: errors landing in the study folder start research; metrics watching triggers sprint planning; workflow-run status changes drive kanban cards and the home-screen live agent feed — all domain-event dispatch.
findings.gap: All existing eventing is terminal-domain and GUI-oriented: Hop-A per-session Channel<TerminalEvent> + global emit/listen, Hop-B pushes, Pv2 §5 byte fan-out. There is no domain-event concept (task-created, error-ingested, run-finished, metric-threshold) and no durable trigger dispatch. Without a named bus, three roadmapped consumers (workflow triggers, S5 'agent-driven card moves render live', S7 stats) plus the home-screen feed each build ad-hoc eventing, and event triggers that fire while the GUI is closed have nowhere durable to land.
findings.recommendation: Name an 'internal domain event bus' component in SW2 (or seed it in S3): typed domain events, durable outbox in the core-owned store, subscriptions from workflow triggers, kanban, and stats. Add one line each to the S5 and S7 rows in overview §3 noting they consume it rather than invent their own.
findings.connectsTo: SW2/V8 (schedule fires = events), V5 (error-ingested events), V19 (metric events), S5/S7, V20's live feed.

findings.title: No shared Tool Registry / StepBinding contract across agents, terminals, and MCP tools
findings.visionNeed: v2: per-step tool bindings ('agents, terminals, MCP tools') interchangeable in workflow steps; agent tool-use; 'custom chains are built from these tools' — a uniform tool abstraction with invoke, streaming progress, result/error, and cost attribution.
findings.gap: No tool abstraction exists anywhere. Three unrelated invocation mechanisms exist or are planned with no unifying contract: the built Hop-B terminal API, the S6a LLM provider trait, and MCP servers (vision-only). The single occurrence of 'tools' in the overview is the S6e row ('prompt+model+tools') with 'tools' undefined. Three future consumers (S6b runtime, S6e custom agents, V1's engine) will each invent their own binding, 'custom chains from these tools' becomes impossible without N adapters, and S6a's per-call cost capture never rolls up to per-step/per-run cost. This is exactly the shared contract a contracts-first project must lock before parallel slices.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Tool Registry (forward contract)' paragraph to overview §4: Tool = {id, source (built-in | MCP server | chain), name, description, JSON-schema input/output, trust class (read-only / spend-bearing / destructive), invoke() with typed errors + scope parameter (see V27), per-call record}. Sources: built-in app tools (terminal ops via Hop-B, kanban/graph/goals APIs), MCP tools (discovered per server), saved chains. SW1 locks a StepBinding contract with three implementations: terminal-worker (Hop-B), app-native agent (S6b runtime), MCP tool (V3). S6e's 'tools' field references registry ids. Lock in the S-MCP spec (first slice that needs it), before S6b. Note in §3 that S6a's cost/token/latency capture attributes to workflow steps so S7 can show $/run.
findings.connectsTo: Owned by V3's slice; consumed by V1's step executor, S6b, S6e; trust classes map to S6c approval classes (V13/V33); S4 retrieval APIs surfaced as built-in tools; cost rollup feeds V25.

findings.title: S6a's locked scope omits LLM tool-calling; LLM-provider vs MCP-tool-provider axes never distinguished
findings.visionNeed: Agents on direct model calls must USE MCP tools (v2 §3), which means LLM tool-use/function-calling: tool definitions in requests, streamed tool_call deltas, dispatch to the MCP server, results fed back — normalized across OpenRouter/OpenAI/GLM.
findings.gap: The S6a row enumerates 'provider trait; adapters; routing + fallback; streaming; retries; per-call capture' — tool-calling is absent (prior audit A8's recommendation listed it but it was dropped when the row was written). Nothing anywhere distinguishes an LLM PROVIDER (model calls) from an MCP TOOL PROVIDER (tool calls) — 'provider' currently means only the former. If S6a ships per its row, its trait lacks tool-def plumbing and streamed tool_call handling → locked-contract rework mid-S6b when agents first need prowl. The conflation risk also runs the other way: 'extending S6a' to talk to MCP servers would entangle model routing/fallback with tool transport that has entirely different semantics (no fallback across tool servers, stateful sessions, different auth).
findings.recommendation: Amend the S6a row now: add 'tool-use/function-calling in the provider trait (tool definitions in requests, streamed tool_call deltas, cross-provider normalization), consuming a Tool Registry it does not own'. Add one sentence to overview §2 locked decisions: 'LLM providers (model calls — S6a) and MCP tool providers (tool calls — S-MCP) are distinct subsystems joined only at the Tool Registry.' Keep the MCP client out of S6a's dependency chain.
findings.connectsTo: V3 supplies the registry (V10); S6b is the first consumer; S7 gets unified per-call records for model calls and tool calls; V28 (sampling) would make S6a the MCP server's counterparty.

findings.title: MCP server registry and credentials have no charter home; BL-20/§16 cover LLM keys only
findings.visionNeed: MCP server registrations (endpoint/command, transport, enabled tools, project scope) are durable domain data; prowl needs an authenticated session/API key; remote servers use API keys or OAuth 2.1 tokens with refresh; interactive authorization is a human-in-the-loop step.
findings.gap: The Data-layer charter partitions data into daemon terminal-domain vs core-owned S3+ domain with no mention of integration/tool-server configs. §16 'Provider API keys (BL-20)' locks Keychain-only + core-process-only egress but is scoped exclusively to LLM provider keys. No doc addresses OAuth token storage/refresh or interactive authorization flows; overview §5's sanctioned human steps don't cover them. Path of least resistance during the MCP slice: a JSON config or SQLite row holding the prowl key — exactly the plaintext trap A9/BL-20 closed for LLM keys.
findings.recommendation: Three amendments in this pass: (a) charter: 'MCP/tool-server registry (servers, transports, enabled tools, project scope) is core-owned S3+ domain data; the daemon never sees it' — with entities McpServerConfig and McpToolCatalogCache (refresh + staleness policy) anticipated by the S3 store decision; (b) generalize §16/BL-20 to 'Provider AND MCP-server credentials (API keys, OAuth tokens, session secrets): macOS Keychain only, never SQLite/config/logs; all integration egress is core-process-only' and retitle BL-20; (c) extend overview §5's 'providing credentials/access' with: interactive OAuth authorization of an MCP server is a one-time sanctioned human step, batched via the S6c inbox. Extend the no-secrets-in-logs test contract to MCP request/response logs.
findings.connectsTo: V3 (the slice this configures), V13 (registration consent), V27 (session state lives beside the registry), BL-2 egress rule, S6c inbox.

findings.title: §16 has no MCP trust boundary: prompt injection via tool results, data egress, stdio code execution, tool spend — all unaddressed
findings.visionNeed: An MCP server is a remote code/data trust boundary: project code, prod error logs, and DB contents flow OUT (the 24h loop researches 'the code, the logs, the database'); untrusted tool results/descriptions flow IN to agents holding terminal execution power; local stdio servers are arbitrary code execution on the owner's machine; metered tools (prowl credits) spend money.
findings.gap: S0+S1 spec §16 covers paths, env, socket, OSC forgery, logging, signing, the agent execution trust layer, SSH agent, provider keys, CSP, data at rest — nothing about external tool servers. Prompt injection via tool results is the canonical MCP attack: a malicious server steers an agent that can execute terminal commands; the §16 gate fires on the resulting command but nothing marks tainted provenance, and list-time tool-description injection poisons every future call. The 24h loop shipping DB rows and source to a third-party server without a consent boundary is silent exfiltration by design — load-bearing for unattended runs where nobody is watching at 3am. Registering a stdio server has no stated consent class.
findings.recommendation: Add an 'MCP boundary' subsection to §16 in this pass (posture now, details in the S-MCP spec): (1) all MCP egress core-process-only (mirrors the LLM rule); (2) per-server data-scope declaration + consent at registration (which projects/data classes may be sent), surfaced in the S6c inbox; (3) tool results AND tool descriptions are UNTRUSTED input — same advisory-never-authoritative class as OSC data — with agent-context provenance recorded; (4) every tool invocation lands in the §16 append-only audit log with args/result digests; (5) spend-bearing tools fall under the existing 'spend/payment' P1 approval class; (6) local stdio server registration requires explicit user trust ack (it is code execution); remote servers pin TLS. Mirror a P1 row into backlog.md so the posture survives until the slice.
findings.connectsTo: Extends (never duplicates) §16's agent trust layer per V34; S6c inbox (consent + spend approvals); BL-2 egress; S7 audit of tool calls; V10's trust classes; V28 (sampling as a spend/egress vector).

findings.title: Data-layer charter lacks the v2 entity map: workflow, MCP, telemetry, and metrics storage is unassigned
findings.visionNeed: v2 adds ~9 entity families with wildly different shapes and volumes: planning CRUD (ideas/tasks/goals), documents (research), append-heavy run/event logs (workflow runs, step states), high-volume dedup streams (prod errors), timeseries (metrics), and config (MCP servers, schedules). The store engine and layout must be chosen against ALL of them, and each family needs an owning slice.
findings.gap: The charter says 'the concrete engine (SQLite vs embedded alternative) is decided in the S3 spec' with only projects/goals/kanban/graph named as the workload. Workflow definitions, trigger state, and run/step history appear nowhere in the charter's enumeration — unassigned, they default into whichever process is convenient (most likely the daemon's bpa.db, a direct charter violation as the only survive-restart component today, or ad-hoc JSON). An engine/layout chosen for planning-CRUD scale can be wrong for run-event logs, error ingestion, and timeseries (write amplification, retention, vacuum). Each later slice bolting on ad-hoc storage is the exact drift the charter exists to stop.
findings.recommendation: Update the charter in this pass with the full entity map + owning slice: DAEMON bpa.db unchanged (sessions, scrollback, terminal-workspaces, command_events). APP-DOMAIN store (engine locked in S3 spec, host process per V2): S3 → Project, Goal, Idea, ResearchArtifact(index), Task, Subtask; S4 → GraphNode, GraphEdge, entity-reference node type; S6a → LlmCallRecord; S-MCP → McpServerConfig, McpToolCatalogCache, McpSessionState, McpCallRecord; SW1/SW2 → WorkflowDefinition (versioned; runs pin the executed version), WorkflowRun, StepState, Trigger/Schedule; prod-feedback → LogSourceConfig, ErrorEvent, StudyItem, DeployRecord; S7/S8 → MetricPoint, Sprint. Rule: S3 sizes the engine against this WHOLE map (SQLite/WAL almost certainly fine; big blobs — research docs, raw log payloads — on the filesystem with DB index rows). Terminal-level evidence stays daemon-side, linked by session_id.
findings.connectsTo: Umbrella for V4/V5/V12/V19/V22 entities; store host decided by V2; migration policy in V15; cross-store refs in V16; telemetry class in V26.

findings.title: App-domain store has no migration policy; WorkflowDefinition has no format versioning
findings.visionNeed: Workflows-as-data, ideas, and metrics are the most schema-volatile data in the product; user-edited WorkflowDefinitions are long-lived documents. The store will migrate constantly and must never eat the owner's workflow library on an upgrade.
findings.gap: Pv2 §7.1 defines a rigorous migration policy (user_version, single transaction, fail-closed, forward-only) for the DAEMON's frozen, terminal-only bpa.db — while the store holding the most-evolving v2 data has none. S3's DoD has only 'export/import round-trips'. No versioning policy exists for the workflow-definition FORMAT: the first S3→S4 schema bump becomes improvisation, and a format change silently breaks saved user workflows.
findings.recommendation: Add to the charter: the app-domain store ships from schema v1 with its own user_version + fail-closed, forward-only, single-transaction migrations — explicitly reuse the daemon's proven persistence.rs machinery as the template. WorkflowDefinition carries a format_version with an append-only evolution rule (mirror the Hop-B 'Protocol evolution & upgrade policy' discipline: additive fields, cross-version decode test per format change). Lock in the S3 spec and workflow-slice spec respectively; S3 export/import doubles as the backup path.
findings.connectsTo: Pv2 §7.1 (reusable template, see V35); V1 (definition format); V14 (the store being versioned).

findings.title: No cross-store reference policy: daemon retention (BL-4) will silently destroy workflow-run evidence
findings.visionNeed: Workflow runs, sprint metrics, and the 24h loop's audit trail must reference terminal sessions and command history DURABLY — 'what did run X execute and with what exit codes' is consumed long after the session ends; v2 makes run history a product feature.
findings.gap: The charter splits storage across two DBs with no cross-reference policy. BL-4 (about to be built with Pv2/S2) purges sessions (20 exited/workspace, 30-day TTL) and Pv2 §7.2 cascades command_events away with their session. App-domain rows will hold SessionIds into bpa.db with no FK possible across DB files: a WorkflowRun older than 30 days points at purged sessions and cascaded-away command_events — dangling refs and an amnesiac audit trail.
findings.recommendation: Add one charter rule NOW, before BL-4 lands: cross-store references are SOFT (UUID strings, no integrity assumption), and the app-domain store is the system of record for run history — on step completion the workflow engine SNAPSHOTS what it needs (the step's command_events slice, exit codes, bounded transcript excerpt) into StepState. Annotate BL-4: daemon retention may purge freely because completed-run evidence is copied out; never extend daemon retention to 'keep sessions referenced by runs' (that would re-couple the stores).
findings.connectsTo: BL-4 (backlog.md), Pv2 §7.2 cascade, V1's StepState model, V32 (the evidence being snapshotted), S7 dashboards consume the same snapshots.

findings.title: Deploy/delivery has no home: no per-project deploy model, deploy step type, or delivery-state surface
findings.visionNeed: v2 §2: fix tasks 'get deployed' — the loop ends with the project deploying its own fixes; the cross-project view always shows per-project 'delivery workflow state'; implied capability: 'delivery/deploy as a workflow step (projects get deployed — the panel must know how)'.
findings.gap: Deploy exists in the docs ONLY as a danger to block (S0S1 spec §16 ~line 892 and docs-truth P1 row list 'production deploy' among S6c approval classes; build-macos.md is the app's own release pipeline). Nothing defines how a MANAGED project deploys: no per-project deploy config (command/script/provider), no deploy-run entity (status, initiator, approval linkage, logs), no rollback posture, no post-deploy hooks, no environments/ops model (where a project runs in production). The loop stops one step short of 'fixed', and V20's delivery lane has nothing to show.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Delivery/deploy step' concept to overview §3/§4: per-project deploy config in the core-owned store (add a small additive 'environments/ops' section to the S3 Project model NOW — log source ref, deploy command/target — so connectors and deploys have an anchor without a later schema break); execution via terminal workers (reuse S1 terminals + Pv2 command_events as the run record — not a CD system, the panel orchestrates the project's own deploy command); gating bound to the EXISTING S6c 'production deploy' approval class; DeployRecord history (what shipped, when, triggered-by run_id). Keep it thin.
findings.connectsTo: V33 (approval class, already designed), V32 (execution+audit substrate), V23 (verification is triggered by deploys), V20 (delivery-state lane), V5/V18 (the loop it completes).

findings.title: Study folder / error-triage queue entity missing — the loop has no memory
findings.visionNeed: v2 §2: errors land in a 'study folder' («папка для изучения») — a durable triage queue with its own lifecycle, feeding research and tracking each error group to resolution.
findings.gap: Named only in the vision doc. S3's data-model row and S5's kanban row have no error-triage entity; the charter's entity list omits it. Error groups need a lifecycle distinct from dev tasks (new → under-research → task-created → fix-deployed → verified / recurred), signature-based dedup so the same crash doesn't spawn N research runs, and links to research artifacts and generated tasks. Without this state machine, verification has nothing to close and recurrences are indistinguishable from new errors.
findings.recommendation: Add the StudyItem entity to the S3/ingestion-slice data model: error-group records keyed by fingerprint signature, status lifecycle, links to research artifacts (S4 graph nodes) and kanban tasks. Raw payload bodies on the filesystem — the literal 'study folder' — with DB index rows. Surface it in the cross-project view as the 'bug-fix tasks' source.
findings.connectsTo: V5 (input), V22 (fix tasks with provenance out), V23 (verification closes/reopens entries), V21 (research artifacts linked), V20 (bug-fix lane).

findings.title: S8 mis-shaped and mis-parked: metrics must be a trigger source that plans sprints, sharing one ingestion substrate with error logs
findings.visionNeed: v2 §2: 'Same mechanism for analytics/metrics watching and sprint planning: the system observes metrics and plans the sprint' — a recurring workflow co-equal with the 24h error loop, with 'Project→Metrics→Sprint' visibility on the panel.

Three problems: (a) shape — it feeds only the CEO as passive context, but v2 makes metrics an active trigger driving a recurring SPRINT-PLANNING workflow; the current DoD is met without any recurring behavior existing; (b) scope — metrics ingestion and prod-error ingestion are the same per-project external-telemetry-pull substrate, at risk of being built twice; no MetricPoint timeseries schema (append-only, retention/downsampling) or Sprint entity exists anywhere; (c) order — parked '(future)' behind S7 though its data dependency is really S3 (S7 only visualizes) and v2 elevates it to flagship status.

Extend DoD: 'a metric-triggered workflow run completes end-to-end, producing a prioritized task set'. Keep S8's provenance DoD — it is exactly right. Note internal sources land earlier: S6a call records and S7 agent stats are the first MetricPoints (V35).
findings.connectsTo: V1/V8 (the recurring workflow + trigger), V5 (shared connector substrate), V9 (metric events), V22 (sprint references tasks), V20 (prioritization + monitoring lanes), CEO planning step in §4.

findings.title: No cross-project control panel / mission-control home; early slices are being built single-project
findings.visionNeed: v2 mission surface: for EVERY project, always visible — goals · plan tasks · bug-fix tasks · prioritization · delivery workflow state · monitoring; home screen with live agent feed across all projects, per-project progress, idea quick-capture, agent-org settings, vector steering, hot questions; north-star 'time-to-context <30 s for all 5–6 projects'. 'The panel is the single place the owner directs all projects from.'

(b) Add slice 'SH — Mission-control home / cross-project control panel' (depends S6c + S7 + the engine's run state): six explicit lanes (goals, plan tasks, bug-fix tasks, cross-project prioritization, delivery/workflow state, monitoring), live agent feed built on Pv2 multi-subscriber attach, idea quick-capture (S3), vector steering (S3 goals), hot questions (S6c inbox), agent-org settings entry (S6e). DoD: cold open answers where-is-every-project + what-needs-me in <30 s. Add the prioritization model (a cross-project ranking spanning ideas/tasks) — currently absent everywhere.
findings.connectsTo: Aggregates S3/S5/S7 + V1 run state; fed by V4 (ideas), V17 (delivery lane), V18 (bug-fix lane), V19 (monitoring/sprint), V33 (hot questions); prioritization altitude reconciled in V22; feed mechanism from V32.

findings.title: S4 has no research-artifact ingest path or programmatic write API — the graph stays a hand-built viz
findings.visionNeed: v2 implied capability: 'research artifacts as durable, linkable objects (feed the knowledge graph)' — outputs of the prowl research step and the self-healing loop's code/logs/DB/docs research become reusable knowledge the CEO retrieves; agents and workflow steps CREATE artifact nodes with provenance.
findings.gap: S4 is a strong foundation (UUID node identity, cross-project links, agent retrieval API) but is specced read/viz-only: no ResearchArtifact node type, no ingest API turning a research run's output into linked nodes, no provenance links back to the originating Idea/WorkflowRun, and nothing says whether non-graph entities (Idea, Task, WorkflowRun) become graph-addressable. S4 hard-blocks S6 (owner decision D6), so a read-only API shape could lock; retrofitting write semantics is avoidable rework, and without a typed entity-reference model S4 either duplicates research content (two sources of truth) or leaves it unlinked (retrieval can't return a goal's research).
findings.recommendation: Amend the S4 row + charter with two locked lines: (1) 'the S4 agent API is read AND write — artifact/document node types with provenance links (idea, workflow run, session)'; extend the DoD: 'a programmatic client stores a research artifact and links it to an idea; retrieval returns it in the idea's subgraph'. (2) Graph nodes may be typed REFERENCES to app-domain entities by shared UUID (node kind = idea|research|task|run|goal + entity_id); UUIDv4 identity discipline shared across the whole app-domain store; the retrieval API resolves reference nodes to entity summaries; physical payloads stay in the S3 store/filesystem — the graph links, never copies. State in the overview that S4 is the durable home for research artifacts, not only a manual viz.
findings.connectsTo: Receives V3's prowl output and V5-loop research; V4's Idea provenance; retrieval feeds the CEO in §4 step 1; UUID discipline shared with V16's soft-ref rule; lands before any agent consumes it per D6.

findings.title: Task model unification: subtasks, task class, priority, multi-source provenance, kanban-as-view
findings.visionNeed: v2: tasks are formed from research, decomposed into SUBTASKS, carry class (plan vs bug-fix) and prioritization; the panel shows them as separate lanes; tasks enter development from multiple sources ('from that research, tasks enter development' — idea pipeline AND error loop); board state must reflect engine-driven work truthfully.
findings.gap: No Task entity is specified anywhere: S5 is board UI (fixed columns, @dnd-kit, drag persists) with nothing stating what a card IS; S3 names Projects+Goals only. Missing: parent/child subtask hierarchy, type (plan|bugfix|chore), priority, provenance FKs (idea/research/workflow-run/error-fingerprint). Overview §4 has exactly one task entry point (CEO from goals+graph) — error-loop and idea-pipeline tasks have no sanctioned path in, and S6b's PM decomposition (which otherwise substantially covers decomposition+design — a partial strength) would lock a goals-only intake. Card-as-free-standing-entity risks board and run state forking ('testing' vs 'failed'). Left unreconciled, v2's ideas/bug-fix/prioritization get crammed into one project's six-column board (wrong altitude — prioritization is cross-project) or duplicated as parallel structures.
findings.recommendation: Move Task/Subtask into the S3 data model (charter update now): Task (project_id, type plan|bugfix|chore, priority, status, parent_task_id, provenance FKs idea_id/research_id/workflow_run_id/error_fingerprint — all nullable). Lock one sentence for S5: 'a Kanban card projects a Task entity; its column derives from task/workflow-run status; agent- and engine-driven moves happen via status change; manual board edits are commands back into the task domain.' Amend §4: tasks enter development from multiple sources (CEO strategy, error-loop research, idea pipeline) with an origin/provenance field carried by the S5 card schema and the S6b PM intake contract. Put PRIORITIZATION at the cross-project panel level (a ranking spanning projects), not inside one board; Ideas sit upstream of Goals — one unified task entity referenced by both board and panel.
findings.connectsTo: V4 (provenance head), V18 (bug-fix tasks born from StudyItems), V19 (Sprint references tasks), V20 (lanes + prioritization), V1 (engine-driven status), S6b PM decomposition (reusable strength to build on).

findings.title: No post-deploy verification step — the loop can mark itself successful dishonestly
findings.visionNeed: v2 §2 net effect: 'the project watches its own production errors and fixes them' — the loop's DoD is that the error actually STOPS, verified against prod; the implied-capabilities list names 'verification'.
findings.gap: No doc mentions post-deploy verification. S7 measures agent-side success/error rates, not prod-side confirmation. Without watching newly ingested events for the fixed error-group's signature over an N-hour window after deploy, the loop can close items that regressed — directly violating the 'honest about state' tenet — and regressed fixes silently rot until the next 24h cycle re-discovers them as 'new'.
findings.recommendation: Spec verification as a first-class workflow step type in the engine slice: bind to (deploy run, error-group signature, watch window); recurrence within the window reopens the StudyItem and escalates to the S6c inbox; success closes it with evidence (zero matching events, window length) recorded in run history.
findings.connectsTo: Requires V5 (data), V18 (signature identity + the entry to close), V17 (deploy trigger); escalates via V33; outcome visible in V25/S7 and V20's monitoring lane.

findings.title: Research source connectors unmodeled: agents querying production DBs/docs need a registry, read-only credentials, and audit
findings.visionNeed: v2 §2: research runs 'over the code, the logs, the database, the project's documentation, the libraries' documentation — wherever needed'.
findings.gap: Code = S2 workspaces (exists); logs = V5's missing ingestion; library docs = Context7 is only a PLANNING-process tool (overview §6), not an agent-runtime capability; the project's production DATABASE and its own docs have no access concept — no per-project source registry, no credential story beyond BL-20's provider-key row. Agents querying a prod DB is the highest-risk research source; left unnamed, S6-era agents will get raw prod credentials ad hoc, violating the project's own security bar against USERS' data.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'research source connectors' item to the workflow/ingestion scope: per-project source registry (repo roots, ingested logs, prod-DB read-only DSN, docs folders, MCP doc/library tools), prod-DB access read-only-by-construction, every query in the §16/S6c audit log; extend BL-20's Keychain rule to per-project source credentials (aligned with V12's generalization).
findings.connectsTo: V12/BL-20 (credential pattern), V13 (egress/audit posture), V3 (library docs and log tools via MCP), V5 (logs source), S6c audit.

findings.title: S7 lacks the workflow-run observability class: scheduled-run health, per-run cost rollup, dead-loop alerts
findings.visionNeed: v2 law #1 (the system pulls the owner in): for unattended 24h loops the owner must be ALERTED when a recurring action fails or silently stops, and unattended spend must stay attributable and bounded.
findings.gap: S7 is scoped to agents and LLM calls (time worked, task counts, errors, traces, spend/budgets; DoD: spend dashboard, per-agent rates, budget alert). Recurring workflows add a class it doesn't name: scheduled-run health (last success, consecutive failures, missed runs), per-WORKFLOW-RUN cost attribution (S6a captures per-call cost but nothing rolls it up per run — a runaway nightly loop burns budget while nobody watches), and a 'recurring action failed/stopped' alert. A silently dead 24h loop is worse than no loop: the owner believes prod is watched when it isn't.
findings.recommendation: Extend the S7 row's scope and DoD: workflow-run health dashboard; 'recurring action failed/missed N times' alert routed to the S6c inbox; per-workflow-run cost rollup built on S6a's per-call records (and McpCallRecords per V34).
findings.connectsTo: V8 run history (data source), V33 (alert channel), S6a cost capture (V35), V20's monitoring lane.

findings.title: Ingested telemetry has no charter data class: no retention, redaction, or purge posture for prod logs carrying user PII/secrets
findings.visionNeed: Ingested prod logs/metrics are potentially the product's largest and most sensitive data volume (prod logs carry USERS' data and secrets) — they need a charter home, retention, and purge rules like every other data class.
findings.gap: The charter defines exactly two buckets (daemon terminal domain; S3+ core-owned store) and its 'historical telemetry' bullet covers only worker transcripts + command_events. Retention exists only for terminal sessions (BL-4); secret hygiene for stored bytes only for scrollback (BL-3: 0600 + purge). Without an amendment, telemetry lands wherever is handy (the drift the charter prevents), grows unboundedly, and persists prod-side PII/secrets with no redaction or purge posture — BL-3 concerns squared, since this is users' data, not the owner's.
findings.recommendation: Amend the charter with a third class — 'ingested telemetry': store home decided in the ingestion slice's spec (core-owned or dedicated store, never bpa.db), size/time-bounded retention windows, redaction posture, purge-on-project-delete; add backlog rows mirroring BL-3/BL-4 for the telemetry class.
findings.connectsTo: V5 (owner slice), V14 (charter map), BL-3/BL-4 (patterns to mirror), S3 store-engine decision.

findings.title: Stateful MCP tool sessions unmodeled: prowl's stable session_id needs a durable, scoped home
findings.visionNeed: v2 names it explicitly: 'prowl session semantics: stable session_id caching per the server's instructions' — the session keeps report cache, conversation history, and circuit-breaker state scoped to one conversation; research spans hours/days and the 24h loop reuses context across a night.
findings.gap: No doc models tool-provider state, and nothing reserves per-server, per-run session state that survives app restarts. If the future tool interface is designed stateless (pure invoke(args)→result — the natural first cut), prowl's cache/circuit-breaker semantics break: every call starts a fresh session, wasting credits and losing the report cache mid-research; retrofitting state into a locked Tool contract breaks every consumer.
findings.recommendation: In the S-MCP spec, include tool session/state from day one: the invocation context carries a scope key (idea-research-run id, workflow-run id, agent-conversation id) and the MCP client persists per-(server, scope) state — McpSessionState, an opaque per-server KV where prowl's session_id lives — in the core store, restored across restarts and expired with the run. The Tool contract (V10) takes an explicit scope parameter so the engine and agent runtime supply it naturally.
findings.connectsTo: V10 (scope parameter in the contract), V4 (research run = the natural scope), V1 (run id), V21 (session state and artifacts share the run scope), V14 (McpSessionState entity).

findings.title: MCP feature surface unbounded; sampling is an unaddressed spend/security decision
findings.visionNeed: 'Connect MCP servers' implies deciding WHICH protocol capabilities the product supports — the protocol also defines resources, prompts, elicitation, and sampling (a server asking the CLIENT for an LLM completion).
findings.gap: No doc bounds the surface. Unbounded, implementers either gold-plate (four subsystems instead of one) or silently drop capabilities users expect. Sampling in particular routes a third-party server's completion requests through the app's own S6a layer — spend on the owner's keys initiated by remote server code; enabled by default it lets a remote server consume the owner's OpenRouter budget.
findings.recommendation: One paragraph in the S-MCP row/spec: v1 surface = tools (list, call, list-changed notifications) + auth/transport; resources/prompts explicitly deferred with a backlog row (per the fix-or-file rule); sampling disabled by default — if ever enabled it routes through S6a with per-server budget caps + the P1 spend approval class. Verify the then-current MCP spec revision via Context7 at spec time (breaking auth changes ship roughly twice a year).
findings.connectsTo: V3 (the slice being bounded), V11 (S6a as sampling's counterparty), V13 (sampling as spend/egress vector), backlog.md.

findings.title: The ideas→research pipeline can ship before the agent org — don't park S-MCP behind S6b–S6e
findings.visionNeed: The first user-visible v2 capability: capture an idea, run prowl research, form a task. It needs the MCP client + an ideas/tasks data model — NOT the full CEO/PM agent org.
findings.gap: With no MCP slice in the graph, the default outcome is it gets appended after the agent-runtime chain, making the flagship v2 pipeline wait behind ~4 slices (provider layer, agent runtime, escalation inbox, worker adapters) it does not depend on. A thin research step — invoke prowl tools, persist artifacts, draft a task — is buildable with only S3 + S-MCP + Keychain, delivering v2 value and de-risking the MCP/Tool contract before agents consume it.
findings.recommendation: When the roadmap is re-cut: place S-MCP with deps {S3, BL-20-pattern secrets} only, parallelizable with S4/S5 (explicitly NOT coupled to Pv2 — core-process outbound, never the Hop-B wire); add an 'Ideas + research pipeline' slice depending on {S3, S-MCP} (not S6b) so it ships before the agent org; S6a/S6b then consume an already-proven tool registry. Update the §3 ASCII dependency graph. D6 (S4 hard-blocks S6) is unaffected — this path routes around S6 entirely.
findings.connectsTo: V3/V4 (the slices being ordered), V10 (contract de-risked early), overview §3 slice table + dependency graph.

findings.title: Overview §1 still states the pre-v2 mission — the framing gap that produced every missing slice
findings.visionNeed: v2 mission as north star: 'take ANY idea to a working project, and manage/organize the vibecoding process' — reflected in the overview's framing so downstream slices inherit the right target.
findings.gap: Overview §1 frames the product as a 'director of AI development teams' setting goals and quality bars — accurate for the ORIGINAL vision but silent on ideas as the entry point, the idea→working-project journey, workflow-as-data, MCP extensibility, and the always-on cross-project panel. A zero-context implementer reading §1 builds an agent-orchestration shell, not an idea-to-project pipeline. This framing gap is WHY the concrete slices (V1, V3, V4, V5, V20) were never in scope.
findings.recommendation: Update §1 to state v2's mission explicitly: 'take any idea to a working project and manage/organize vibecoding across all projects'; name the idea→[research]→task→subtasks→design→dev pipeline, the editable workflow-as-data engine, MCP servers as the extension mechanism, and the always-visible cross-project control panel (goals/tasks/bugs/prioritization/delivery/monitoring). This anchors every slice this register adds.
findings.connectsTo: Umbrella framing for V1–V5, V20; pairs with V20's adoption of the three north-star metrics into §1.

findings.title: Pv2 loose ends that v2 makes load-bearing: additive-request ownership, command_events attribution, frozen preamble
findings.visionNeed: Workflow steps and agents driving terminals deterministically (command+argv spawn, typed exit-status wait, ReadOutput{since_seq}, rendered-text snapshot); run/audit attribution of what ran in which session; future agent/MCP caller identity — over a wire Pv2 is about to freeze.
findings.gap: Verdict: Pv2 does NOT contradict v2 — append-only variants + negotiation mean everything can land additively later; nothing must be crammed into Pv2 now. Residual gaps: (a) the four additive agent requests exist only in overview §4 as 'planned' with no owning cycle, yet they now GATE the workflow engine's terminal steps; (b) command_events (session_id, seq, ts, kind, exit_code) lacks command text and caller/run attribution — workflow history + S7 will force a schema v3 bump one or two cycles after v2; (c) the §4.2 preamble is 'raw, never changes', so identity can never ride there — undocumented, someone may try.
findings.recommendation: Three one-line amendments while Pv2 is in design: (1) name a 'Pv2.1 additive batch' in overview §4 owned by the workflow-engine slice (SW1) for the four requests; (2) note planned command_events v3 columns in Pv2 §7 (cmdline from OSC-133 where available, caller/run tag) — or add a nullable cmdline column now since the schema is breaking anyway; (3) add one sentence to §4.2: 'future identity/attribution fields ride in CBOR frames; the preamble is frozen forever.'
findings.connectsTo: V1 (terminal steps gated by the additive batch), V32 (the substrate these complete), V16 (command_events as snapshotted evidence), S6b/S6c audit trail, BL-4 cascade, the protocol-evolution policy.

findings.title: REUSABLE: Hop-B socket + command_events + multi-subscriber attach are the workflow engine's terminal-step substrate — direct reuse, forbid reinvention
findings.visionNeed: Workflow steps that spawn/drive terminals (build/test/deploy steps, external coding agents as step workers), per-step run evidence, and the owner co-watching a workflow's terminal live (home-screen feed).
findings.gap: No design gap — an ownership/framing gap with reinvention risk: overview §4 already locks the Hop-B socket as the canonical programmatic agent API (create/attach/write-stdin/stream/resize/kill/query-state); Pv2 §5 ships multi-subscriber attach (N subscribers, own Replay + backpressure) and §7 ships command_events (command started/finished + exit_code from OSC-133, written by the daemon from day one). A workflow-engine spec written without these pointers will build its own step executor, status capture, and telemetry parallel to the daemon.
findings.recommendation: State in overview §4 and the future SW1/SH specs: the engine's terminal-step executor drives Hop-B directly (same socket client as agents); terminal-step runs bind to a daemon session_id and consume command_events + typed exit-status wait as the step-status source of truth (command+argv spawn = deterministic execution, no shell-injection surface); live tap / owner co-watch / home feed = additional attach subscribers. Assign the four additive capabilities to SW1's dependency list (V31). Forbid parallel bespoke channels in those specs' non-goals. Combine with V16's snapshot-on-completion rule so evidence survives daemon retention.
findings.connectsTo: V1 (step executor), V17 (deploy run record), V31 (Pv2.1 batch), V16 (snapshots), V20 (live feed), S6d worker adapters use the same subscriptions, S7 step-level timing from the same events.

findings.title: REUSABLE: S6c approval inbox IS v2's hot-questions queue and the unattended loop's human gate — bind to it, extend it, don't fork it
findings.visionNeed: v2 law #3: autonomy default, approvals wait in ONE inbox; the deploy step of an unattended 24h run must park safely until approved; hot questions on the home screen come from one queue, not N terminal tabs.
findings.gap: No mismatch — already designed: S0S1 spec §16 + docs-truth define approval classes (including 'production deploy'), batched inbox, full audit log, implemented in S6c. Deltas only: intake breadth (currently reads as agent-escalations only), multi-project scope, per-project/per-environment policy knobs (e.g. auto-deploy staging, approval-required prod), and durable suspend/resume so an unattended run parked on approval survives host restarts. The risk is the workflow engine growing a parallel gate.
findings.recommendation: In the workflow-engine spec: deploy/destructive/spend steps route through the S6c approval classes verbatim; extend the class table with per-project/per-environment policy; define 'awaiting-approval' as a durable workflow-run state (persisted with the run, resumed by inbox action). Amend the S6c row: intake sources include workflow human-approval STEPS and policy gates (spend, destructive ops, spec approvals), and the inbox is the single queue across ALL projects; SH/V20 surfaces it as the hot-questions widget rather than building its own.
findings.connectsTo: V7 (generic gate framing), V8 (suspend/resume semantics), V17 (deploy gating), V13 (MCP consent/spend approvals land here too), V20 (hot-questions widget), v2 north-star metric (b).

findings.title: REUSABLE: §16 trust layer, S6a cost capture, and BL-20 Keychain generalize to MCP verbatim; plus a P3 backlog idea — expose the app AS an MCP server
findings.visionNeed: v2 needs the product to DRIVE external tool servers; it was already built to BE driven, and the existing security/observability patterns are the right chassis for the MCP client.
findings.gap: Four locked pieces already fit but none say they generalize: (1) overview §4's Hop-B canonical API makes the app a headless-drivable engine, architecturally MCP-adjacent; (2) §16's agent execution trust layer (approval classes incl. spend/payment, batched inbox, append-only audit, caller identity) is a generic dangerous-action interception layer, not terminal-specific; (3) S6a's 'per-call cost/token/latency capture from the first call' applies verbatim to metered tool calls; (4) §16/BL-20 'Keychain only + egress core-only' is a general integration-credential posture. A zero-context S-MCP implementer would plausibly build a parallel consent dialog, a second secrets path, and its own call-metrics table — three duplicated subsystems and a fragmented audit trail.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit cross-references in this pass: §16's trust-layer subsection gains 'this layer also gates MCP tool invocations (spend-bearing/destructive tool classes)'; the S6a cost-capture bullet gains '(the same record discipline applies to MCP tool calls — McpCallRecord mirrors LlmCallRecord; S7 unifies model spend and tool spend)'; BL-20 generalized per V12. Separately file ONE backlog idea row (P3, not roadmap): expose the app itself as an MCP server (its Hop-B capabilities as MCP tools) so external agents like Claude Code can drive Builder Pro — nearly free once the Hop-B surface is stable.
findings.connectsTo: Prevents duplicate trust/secrets/metrics subsystems across V3, S6a, S6c, S7; V12/V13 implement the generalized rules; the app-as-MCP-server idea connects §4's forward contract to the broader agent ecosystem.

findings.title: REUSABLE: S6a/MCP call records are the first MetricPoint sources; persistence.rs is the migration-machinery template
findings.visionNeed: v2 metrics→sprint planning needs metric history that cannot be backfilled — capture must start with the first call; the app-domain store needs proven migration machinery, not a new design.
findings.gap: No mismatch — call-outs so the corrected plan reuses rather than reinvents: (a) S6a already locks 'per-call cost/token/latency capture from the first call'; LlmCallRecord and McpCallRecord are the FIRST MetricPoint sources — the metrics store should ingest them, not run a second capture path; (b) the daemon's persistence.rs migration machinery (user_version, fail-closed, single transaction — Pv2 §7.1) and S3's export/import DoD are proven patterns to transplant.
findings.recommendation: In the corrected roadmap, mark S6a call records as an internal metrics source feeding the S7/S8 timeseries, and reference persistence.rs as the migration-machinery template in the S3 spec's storage section (per V15).
findings.connectsTo: V19 (MetricPoint/Sprint), V15 (migration policy), V25 (cost rollup), V34 (McpCallRecord mirrors LlmCallRecord).

findings.title: Overview §5's sanctioned human steps omit workflow authoring/editing
findings.visionNeed: v2 makes authoring/editing workflows (steps, order, schedules, bindings) a core, sanctioned owner activity ('change the flow and keep it flexible for himself'), alongside home-screen vector steering.
findings.gap: Overview §5: 'The only sanctioned human steps: setting/adjusting goals + quality bars, answering batched escalations, and providing credentials/access. Everything else is agent-decided.' Taken literally, §5 brands workflow editing out-of-contract — and §5 is normative language other slices cite.
findings.recommendation: Add 'authoring and editing workflow definitions, schedules, and step bindings' to §5's sanctioned human steps (V12 separately adds one-time MCP authorization).
findings.connectsTo: SW3 editor UI (V1), V12 (the parallel §5 amendment), v2 home-screen vector steering (V20).

uxRaw.scenario: Idea → working project (Builder Pro AI Vision v2). The owner captures a raw idea at 1am, spawns a new project from it, triggers prowl.chat market research, reviews the durable research artifact, approves an AI-formed task breakdown, steers the brainstorm→spec→plan design workflow through exactly the approvals that matter, and watches development start in real terminals — all from the home control panel, with every wait state batched into the single approval inbox instead of polling. Target behavior for the S3–S6 slices plus the new Idea/Research/Workflow subsystems implied by Vision v2.
userJourney: 1. OPEN — Owner opens the app. Home screen renders in <30s of context: live agent feed (every agent, every stage, every project), per-project progress rows, the Hot Questions inbox badge (e.g. '3'), and a persistent Idea quick-capture field in the top bar (also global hotkey ⌘⇧I from anywhere in macOS).

2. CAPTURE — Owner types a raw idea into quick-capture: 'AI changelog writer that reads merged PRs and drafts release notes'. Presses Enter. A lightweight capture sheet slides out — the raw text is already saved (nothing is lost even if he closes the sheet); the sheet only asks for routing.

3. ROUTE — The sheet shows two big choices: 'Attach to project…' (typeahead list of his 5-6 active projects, most-recently-touched first) or 'Spawn new project'. He picks Spawn new project. Inline mini-form appears: suggested project name (LLM-suggested from the idea text, editable), optional workspace root ('create repo later' is the default — no filesystem decision forced at capture time). He confirms. Toast: 'Idea captured → new project Changelog-AI'. The home screen gains a new project row with a seedling badge (project state: incubating).

4. RESEARCH DECISION — The idea card opens (or he clicks it later from the project's Idea inbox). Card shows: raw text, status chip 'captured', and an optional 'Run research' section: scope checkboxes (competitive / market / SEO), depth (quick scan vs full report), and an estimated cost + time chip (prowl call budget). He checks competitive + market and clicks 'Start research'. Because research has spend, the button shows the cost estimate inline — clicking it IS the spend approval (no second dialog).

5. WAIT/STREAM — The idea card flips to 'researching' with a live streaming pane: prowl status lines and partial findings stream in as they arrive ('found 4 direct competitors…', 'pulling SERP data for release notes automation…'). Critically, he does NOT have to watch: he navigates back home, where the live agent feed now shows a row 'Changelog-AI · Research · prowl running (3m)'. He goes to bed / another project. If research fails, it retries per policy and only then lands one item in Hot Questions ('Research failed after 3 attempts — retry / skip / change scope?').

6. RESEARCH DONE — Next time he opens the app (or via the batched notification), the project row shows 'Research ready ✦'. He clicks through to the Research Artifact view: a rendered report (competitors table, market sizing, SEO keyword opportunities, sources with links), a 'key findings' chip strip, and a provenance footer (prowl session, tools invoked, cost actually spent). Actions: Accept, Refine (free-text follow-up question → incremental prowl call on the same session), Re-run, Discard. He clicks Accept.

7. TASK FORMATION — On Accept, the PM agent (app-native) synthesizes idea + research into a proposed Task: title, one-paragraph objective, acceptance criteria, and a decomposed Subtask tree (e.g. 'GitHub PR ingestion', 'summarization prompt + eval', 'release-notes template engine', 'publish step'). The owner lands on the Breakdown Review screen: an editable tree — drag to reorder, inline-edit titles/criteria, delete, add, set priority. Each subtask shows the specialist role it will be assigned to.

8. APPROVE BREAKDOWN — He tweaks two subtasks, then clicks 'Approve & start design'. This is a policy-gated approval (P1) — approving inline here is the same act as approving from the Hot Questions inbox; either surface clears the item. Kanban for Changelog-AI now shows the subtasks as backlog cards. Idea status chip advances: captured → researched → specced-pending.

9. DESIGN WORKFLOW RUNS — The design workflow (a workflow-as-data definition: brainstorm → spec → plan, visible and editable in the project's Workflow tab) starts a run. He can open the Workflow Run timeline: step chips with states (done / running / waiting-approval / queued). Brainstorm step: the PM agent generates 4 clarifying questions. They do NOT interrupt him — they arrive as ONE batched card in Hot Questions ('Changelog-AI design: 4 questions'). He answers all four in a single sitting in the inbox (radio options + free text), submits once.

10. SPEC GATE — The spec step runs unattended using his answers + the research artifact + project goals. When the spec doc is written, a Hot Questions item appears: 'Spec ready for approval — Changelog-AI'. He opens the spec review surface: rendered doc with a diff-style highlight of locked contracts (types, file layout), plus 'Approve / Request changes (with comment)'. He requests one change ('use webhooks, not polling'); the PM revises within the same run; second review — he approves. This is the ONE intervention that matters (north-star metric).

11. PLAN — The plan step runs fully autonomously (policy: plans don't gate by default; he could add a gate by editing the workflow). The Workflow Run timeline shows 'plan: done', with the plan doc linkable from the run.

12. DEV STARTS — Development begins without him touching anything: engineering specialist agents claim subtasks; each spawns a terminal worker (claude-code) in the project's workspace. If he chose 'create repo later' at capture, the first dev step scaffolds the repo (git init, CI, gates) as its own workflow step and binds it as the project's workspace root. On home, the live agent feed shows 'Changelog-AI · backend-specialist → claude-code · implementing PR ingestion (12m)'. Kanban cards move backlog → todo → progress live.

13. STEER (OPTIONAL) — At any point he can: (a) click a feed row to co-view the actual terminal session read-only alongside the agent (multi-subscriber attach), (b) open the project and edit goals/priorities — the Vector Steering panel — which the CEO/PM pick up on their next decision loop, (c) toss more ideas into the same project's backlog from quick-capture. None of this is required for progress.

14. ESCALATIONS ONLY — Over the next hours, the only things that reach him are batched Hot Questions items (e.g. 'worker wedged on GitHub API auth — needs a token' → he pastes a credential once). Everything else proceeds. Subtask cards flow progress → testing → done as workers finish and gates pass.

15. SHIPPED — When the last subtask hits done and the final verification step passes, the task completes; the idea's lifecycle chip reads 'shipped'. The home row for Changelog-AI shows a green pulse + summary ('shipped: v0.1 changelog writer · 1 human intervention · $4.12 spend'). The idea card forever links: raw idea → research artifact → task → spec → plan → commits → deploy — the full provenance chain in the knowledge graph.
dataFlow: 1. OPEN — No writes. Core process reads the core-owned store (SQLite in core, per Data-layer charter): projects, ideas, tasks, workflow runs, escalations. In parallel the GUI's socket client attaches to the daemon (Hop-B) to rehydrate live terminal sessions for the agent feed. Daemon store (bpa.db) is touched only for terminal-domain state — session records, scrollback replay. Renderer state assembled in Zustand.

2. CAPTURE — Actor: the GUI (no agent yet). Core store: INSERT Idea{id, raw_text, created_at, status:'captured', project_id:NULL}. Written immediately on Enter (crash-safe before routing). Audit log entry 'idea.captured'.

3. ROUTE/SPAWN — Actor: GUI + one small app-native LLM call (S6a provider layer) for the name suggestion (logged with cost like every call). Core store, one transaction: INSERT Project{id, name, state:'incubating', workspace_roots:[]}; UPDATE Idea.project_id; INSERT knowledge-graph nodes (S4): IdeaNode + ProjectNode + edge idea→project. No daemon involvement — no workspace/terminal exists yet.

4. RESEARCH TRIGGER — Actor: workflow engine (core) instantiates a ResearchRun from the built-in 'idea-research' workflow definition (workflow-as-data, stored in core store as WorkflowDef rows). Core store: INSERT WorkflowRun{def:'idea-research', idea_id, status:'queued'} + INSERT ResearchRun{scope:[competitive,market], budget_est}. UPDATE Idea.status='researching'. The spend approval is recorded as a pre-approved policy token on the run (audit: 'spend.approved inline, $est'). The MCP client subsystem (core-resident, per Vision v2 implied capability) resolves the prowl server connection and loads/creates the per-project prowl session_id from core store (McpSession table — prowl requires a stable session_id across calls).

5. STREAMING — Actor: MCP client subsystem invoking prowl_analyze (egress is core-only, consistent with the S6a rule that all network leaves from core). Streaming/status events are appended to core store table research_events{run_id, seq, payload} (append-only, replayable — same pattern as terminal scrollback but core-owned, NOT in the daemon's bpa.db). GUI subscribes via Tauri event channel; the idea card and the home feed row are both projections of the same event stream. On failure: retry counter on ResearchRun; after policy exhaustion INSERT Escalation{kind:'research_failed'} into core store — which is what the Hot Questions inbox renders.

6. ARTIFACT — Actor: MCP client finalizes the run. Core store: INSERT ResearchArtifact{id, idea_id, project_id, report_md (blob), findings_json, sources[], prowl_session_id, cost_actual}; UPDATE ResearchRun.status='done', WorkflowRun step advance; UPDATE Idea.status='researched'. Knowledge graph (S4): ArtifactNode + typed nodes for extracted entities (CompetitorNode, KeywordCluster) with edges to IdeaNode/ProjectNode — this is 'research artifacts feed the knowledge graph'. 'Refine' issues another prowl call on the SAME session_id and versions the artifact (artifact_revisions).

7. TASK FORMATION — Actor: PM app-native agent (S6b runtime, runs in core, LLM via S6a with per-call cost capture). Reads: Idea + ResearchArtifact + project goals + graph retrieval API (S4 — the <100ms subgraph query). Writes to core store: INSERT Task{id, idea_id, research_artifact_id, project_id, status:'draft', acceptance_criteria} + INSERT Subtask rows {task_id, order, role_assignment, status:'draft'}. Kanban cards are NOT duplicated entities — each Subtask projects into an S5 backlog card (card = view of subtask row). Graph edges task→idea, task→artifact.

8. BREAKDOWN APPROVAL — Actor: owner via GUI; trust layer (S6c). Owner edits write directly to Subtask rows (versioned edits, audit-logged). 'Approve & start design': INSERT Approval{kind:'breakdown', task_id, actor:'owner'} in core store; resolve the pending Escalation if it was surfaced in the inbox; UPDATE Task.status='approved'; UPDATE Idea.status→'specced-pending'. This approval event is the trigger the workflow engine listens for.

9. DESIGN WORKFLOW / BRAINSTORM — Actor: workflow engine starts WorkflowRun{def:'design-pipeline'} (brainstorm→spec→plan steps from the editable WorkflowDef). Brainstorm step binds to the PM agent (per-step tool binding: agent | terminal | MCP tool). PM generates questions → core store: INSERT Escalation{kind:'design_questions', payload:[4 questions], batch:true}. Owner's answers: UPDATE Escalation.resolution + append to the run's context record; step state waiting-approval→done. Every state transition of every step is a row in workflow_step_events (run history is first-class, per Vision v2 §2).

10. SPEC GATE — Actor: PM agent writes the spec. The spec doc is dual-homed by design: canonical file in the repo when a workspace exists, ALWAYS mirrored as a SpecArtifact blob in core store (so specs exist for repo-less incubating projects — this project may still have no repo). If a repo exists, a terminal worker (or core FS write) commits it. Core store: INSERT SpecArtifact{task_id, version, content}; INSERT Escalation{kind:'spec_approval'}. 'Request changes' → INSERT review comment, step loops (spec v2), second Escalation; 'Approve' → INSERT Approval{kind:'spec'}, step done. All P1-class per S6c, all in the audit log.

11. PLAN — Actor: PM agent, unattended. Core store: INSERT PlanArtifact{task_id, content, spec_version}; workflow step brainstorm/spec/plan all 'done'; UPDATE Task.status='ready-for-dev'. No escalation created (policy: plan step has no gate unless the owner edits the WorkflowDef to add one).

12. DEV START — Actors chain: workflow engine advances to the dev step → engineering specialist agents (app-native, core) claim Subtasks (UPDATE Subtask.assignee, status:'in-progress' → kanban card moves live) → each specialist drives a terminal worker via the daemon socket API (Hop-B: create session, spawn claude-code, write-stdin, stream-output). NOW the daemon store gets its first rows for this project: session records + scrollback in bpa.db (terminal domain only — the daemon never sees Task/Idea entities). If no repo existed: a 'scaffold' workflow step runs first — terminal worker does git init + gates; core store UPDATE Project.workspace_roots+=[path] (additive workspace_roots per A14); graph WorkspaceNode. Worker liveness watched by the S6d adapter (claude-code strategy), not waiting_for_input.

13. STEERING — (a) Co-view: GUI attaches as a second subscriber to the worker's session (protocol v2 multi-subscriber attach, owner decision D5); read-only projection, no entity writes, audit row 'session.coviewed'. (b) Vector steering: owner edits Goal rows in core store (S3); CEO/PM agents re-read goals + graph on their next loop — no push mechanism needed, the loop is the propagation. (c) New ideas: same flow as step 2, Idea rows with project_id set, appearing as backlog kanban cards after triage.

14. ESCALATION LOOP — Actor: S6d worker adapter detects wedge → INSERT Escalation{kind:'worker_stuck', session_ref} (core store; the escalation references the daemon session id but lives in core). Owner's credential answer: secret goes to Keychain (BL-20 — NEVER a core-store row), Escalation resolved, specialist agent feeds the unblock into the worker session via write-stdin. Subtask completions: worker exit-status + gate results → specialist UPDATEs Subtask.status through testing→done; kanban and home feed are projections; workflow_step_events append throughout.

15. SHIPPED — Actor: workflow engine's final verification step (runs gates via a terminal worker; deploy is itself a workflow step per Vision v2 'delivery/deploy as a workflow step'). Core store final transaction: UPDATE Task.status='done'; UPDATE Idea.status='shipped'; UPDATE Project.state='active'; WorkflowRun closed with full run history; Stats (S7) aggregates per-call LLM costs + intervention count into the shipped summary. Knowledge graph now holds the complete provenance chain idea→artifact→task→spec→plan→workspace, queryable by the CEO for future decisions.
