Idea inbox: per-project list + cross-project view; idea cards with lifecycle chips (captured → researched → specced → in-dev → shipped)
Idea detail card with the optional 'Run research' section: scope/depth pickers, inline cost-estimate chip that doubles as spend approval
Research streaming pane (live prowl status/finding events, replayable) + the corresponding compact row in the home live-agent feed
Research Artifact viewer: rendered report, key-findings chips, sources, provenance/cost footer, Accept / Refine (same-session follow-up) / Re-run / Discard actions, revision history
Breakdown Review screen: editable task/subtask tree (reorder, inline edit, add/delete, priority, role-assignment preview) with Approve & start design
Workflow Run timeline view: step chips with live states (queued / running / waiting-approval / done), links to produced artifacts, full run history
Workflow definition editor (workflow-as-data): view/edit the design pipeline steps, add gates, reorder, bind tools per step (agent | terminal worker | MCP tool)
Spec review surface: rendered spec with locked-contracts highlighting, Approve / Request-changes-with-comment loop
Hot Questions inbox extensions: batched design-question cards (multi-question single-submit), spec-approval items, research-failure items, worker-stuck items with credential handoff
Co-view terminal: read-only second-subscriber attach to a worker session from the agent feed (protocol v2 D5)
Vector Steering panel: per-project goals/priorities editor whose changes agents pick up on their next loop
MCP Servers settings page: connect/authorize servers (prowl first), per-project session status, spend visibility

Backend capabilities: Idea / ResearchRun / ResearchArtifact / Task / Subtask / WorkflowDef / WorkflowRun / Escalation / Approval schemas in the CORE-owned store (never bpa.db); MCP client subsystem in core with persisted per-project prowl session_id; workflow engine with scheduler, event triggers, per-step tool bindings, append-only step-event history; PM decomposition + spec/plan authoring under the S6b runtime; subtask→kanban-card projection (S5); graph node/edge writers for idea/artifact/task provenance (S4); S6c approval classes covering breakdown/spec/spend; S6d adapter escalation for wedged workers; Keychain-only credential handoff
openQuestions: Approval-gate defaults: is breakdown approval (step 8) a hard P1 gate like spec approval, or policy-configurable per project (auto-proceed for small tasks)? Vision v2 targets ~1 intervention per shipped task — two mandatory gates already exceeds it.
Research auto-run policy: can a project policy make research run automatically on idea capture (no step-4 click), and what spend ceiling applies before it must escalate instead?

ResearchArtifact canonical home: core-store blob only, or also materialized as a markdown file in the repo once a workspace exists (like specs are dual-homed)? Affects greppability by terminal workers.

Repo bootstrap ownership for spawned projects: which workflow step scaffolds the repo (template choice, gates, CI), and can the owner defer it past spec approval — i.e. can dev start be blocked solely on 'no workspace yet'?

prowl session semantics: one stable session_id per PROJECT vs per IDEA — per-project keeps report cache/context across ideas but risks cross-idea bleed in refine calls; needs a locked decision before the MCP client subsystem spec.

Subtask ↔ kanban card identity: the scenario assumes card = projection of Subtask row (one entity). Confirm S5 spec doesn't require independent card entities (manual cards with no subtask would then need a separate type).

Failure degradation for the MCP path: if prowl is down/unauthorized, does the pipeline offer a degraded 'skip research, form task from idea only' path inline, and how is the honest-degradation notice recorded on the artifact chain?

Idea triage for attach-to-existing: do attached ideas land straight in backlog kanban, or in a per-project idea-triage queue the PM agent grooms on a schedule (touches the recurring-actions mechanism)?

Sequencing vs roadmap: Idea/Research/Workflow entities need S3 (core store) + S6a (LLM+MCP egress) + S6b (PM agent); does the idea-capture UI (steps 1-6, no agents) ship earlier as an S3-adjacent slice, with task formation arriving at S6b?

Cost attribution: prowl spend and meta-agent LLM spend both roll into S7 budgets — per-idea and per-task rollups needed, and does a project budget ceiling pause a running WorkflowRun (and as which escalation kind)?

uxRaw.scenario: Build & edit a custom workflow — the owner composes the 24h prod-error self-healing chain in the visual workflow editor, binds each step to an executor (app-native agent, terminal worker, or MCP tool), saves and enables it, fires a manual run, watches the step-by-step run, answers the one deploy approval in the Hot-questions inbox, and later edits the live workflow by inserting a Slack-notify step (creating definition v2 while in-flight runs stay pinned to v1). Grounded in the Builder Pro AI architecture: WorkflowDefinition/Step/Trigger/ToolBinding/WorkflowRun/StepRun all live in the CORE-owned store (per the Data-layer charter the daemon owns terminal-domain state only); the workflow engine + scheduler run in the core process; terminal steps execute as daemon-owned PTY sessions over the Hop-B socket; MCP steps go through the core MCP client (egress core-only); policy-gated steps block on the S6c approval inbox. This is TARGET behavior — the workflow engine is an implied capability of Vision v2, not yet a built slice.
userJourney: Step 1 — Open the editor: from the home screen sidebar the owner clicks 'Workflows' inside the project 'oxdev'. He sees the workflow list: built-in read-only templates (Dev workflow: brainstorm→spec→plan→subagent-dev) and his custom workflows, each row showing name, enabled/disabled pill, next-run time, last-run status dot (green/red/amber), and 24h cost. He clicks '+ New workflow'.

Step 2 — Name & scope: a creation sheet asks for name ('Prod error self-healing'), description, and scope (this project / all projects). He picks project-scoped. The editor opens: an @xyflow/react canvas (same component family as the S4 graph) with a single Trigger placeholder node on the left, a right-hand Inspector panel, and a top bar with Save / Enable toggle (greyed until valid) / Run now / Version badge 'draft v1'.

Step 3 — Configure the trigger: he clicks the Trigger node. The Inspector shows trigger types: Schedule (cron), Event (e.g. 'error-rate spike', 'deploy finished'), Manual only, Webhook. He picks Schedule, chooses the preset 'Every 24h' which expands to an editable cron ('0 3 * * *', runs 03:00 local), and sees a computed 'Next run: tomorrow 03:00' preview plus a concurrency policy dropdown (if previous run still active: Skip / Queue / Cancel-previous) — he picks Skip.

Step 4 — Add step 1 'Ingest prod error logs': he drags a Step node from the palette onto the canvas and connects Trigger→Step. In the Inspector he names it, then opens the Tool binding picker — a three-tab chooser: Agents (app-native org roles from S6e registry), Terminals (command templates run as daemon PTY workers), MCP tools (tools discovered from connected MCP servers). He picks Terminal, selects the project's saved command template 'fetch-prod-logs --since 24h', and sets the step's declared output: 'artifact: error-log bundle → Study folder'. A schema chip appears on the node's output port.

Step 5 — Add step 2 'Research': he adds the next node, connects it, and binds an Agent — the app-native 'Research' role (model + prompt from agent-org settings). In the binding config he checks the retrieval sources this agent may use for this step: workspace code (S2 roots), the incoming Study-folder artifact, the project database (read-only connection from project settings), project docs + knowledge graph (S4 retrieval API), library docs. He also toggles on one MCP tool the agent may call: prowl (prowl_analyze, with the project's stable session_id shown as inherited from project MCP settings). Declared output: 'Research report artifact + proposed fixes list'.

Step 6 — Add step 3 'Form fix tasks': binds the app-native PM agent. Config: input = research report; action template = 'decompose into bug-fix tasks'; output = 'Kanban cards in column Backlog, tagged bugfix + provenance link to the research artifact'. The Inspector previews the card fields so he can see exactly what will appear on the S5 board.

Step 7 — Add step 4 'Run dev workflow': from the palette he drags a Sub-workflow node and points it at the built-in 'Dev workflow' definition, parameterized with 'tasks = output of step 3'. The node renders collapsed with a 'contains 4 stages' badge; clicking it peeks into the child definition read-only. Fan-out policy: 'one child run per task, max 2 parallel'.

Step 8 — Add step 5 'Deploy': binds a Terminal command template 'deploy-prod' from project settings. The moment he selects it, the editor auto-flags the node with an amber shield: 'Policy-gated: destructive/production — will pause for approval'. He opens the gate config and keeps the default (require approval, batchable, timeout 12h → fail run) rather than granting standing auto-approve.

Step 9 — Add step 6 'Verify': binds the Verification agent with config 'watch prod logs + health endpoint for 30 min post-deploy; success = error signature from step 1 absent AND no new criticals'. On-failure policy dropdown: Escalate + offer rollback (default) — he keeps it. He wires Deploy→Verify and the chain is complete: Trigger → Ingest → Research → Form tasks → Dev workflow → Deploy → Verify.

Step 10 — Validate & save: the top-bar 'Save' is now active because the validation panel shows all green: every step has a binding, every edge's output/input schema chips match, the gated step has an owner-visible policy, cost estimate per run is displayed (from S6a per-call pricing: ~$4–9/run). He clicks Save. Toast: 'Prod error self-healing v1 saved (disabled)'. The workflow appears in the list, pill grey.

Step 11 — Enable: he flips the Enable toggle. A confirm sheet restates what will happen autonomously ('runs nightly 03:00; only Deploy waits for you; est. cost/run') — he confirms. Pill turns green; 'Next run: 03:00' appears on the list row and on the home screen's per-project progress card for oxdev.

Step 12 — Run now: instead of waiting he clicks 'Run now'. The view switches to the Run detail screen: a vertical timeline of StepRuns, each with state chip (queued/running/waiting-approval/succeeded/failed/skipped), live duration, live cost, and an expandable body. Step 1 shows an embedded live terminal (he is co-viewing the same PTY the engine drives, via multi-subscriber attach). Step 2 then streams the Research agent's reasoning/tool-calls, including a prowl call with its cost line. Step 3 posts 3 Kanban cards — the run view shows them as chips that deep-link to the board. Step 4 shows the collapsed child-run tree (3 child dev-workflow runs, 2 running / 1 queued) with drill-in.

Step 13 — Approve the deploy: when step 5 is reached the run pauses; the node shows 'Waiting for you' and a card lands in the Hot-questions inbox on the home screen (and a macOS notification fires): 'Prod error self-healing: approve deploy to prod — 3 fixes, diff summary, tests green, est. impact'. He opens the card, reviews the batched context (diffs, test results, the originating error signatures), clicks Approve. The run resumes without him navigating anywhere; step 5's terminal streams the deploy, step 6's Verify agent reports 'error signature gone, 0 new criticals' 30 min later, and the run flips to Succeeded. The home screen agent-feed entry collapses to a green line.

Step 14 — Edit the live workflow (add Slack notify): two days later he opens the workflow, clicks 'Edit'. The editor opens a new draft (v2) — the enabled v1 keeps running untouched. He drags a Step node after Verify, names it 'Notify Slack', opens the binding picker → MCP tab. Slack MCP isn't connected yet, so the tab shows 'Connect a server' → he adds the Slack MCP server in the app's MCP registry (auth flow), returns, and binds tool 'send_message' with channel '#oxdev-prod' and a message template referencing run outputs ('{{run.summary}} — {{steps.verify.result}}'). He also sets it to run on BOTH success and failure paths.

Step 15 — Publish v2: Save → 'Publish v2?' sheet shows a structural diff (+1 step, 1 new MCP dependency) and the rule: 'in-flight runs finish on v1; runs started after publish use v2'. He publishes. The list row now reads v2; the version badge history (v1, v2 with timestamps and 'restore' actions) is available from the workflow's History tab.

Step 16 — Review run history: he opens the workflow's Runs tab: a table of WorkflowRuns (trigger source: schedule/manual, start, duration, status, cost, definition version). He clicks last night's scheduled run and replays it step-by-step: per-StepRun timing, full terminal scrollback for terminal steps, agent transcripts + LLM trace/cost for agent steps, MCP request/response for tool steps, artifacts (study-folder bundle, research report) as durable linkable objects wired into the knowledge graph, and the approval record (who/when) on the deploy step. This satisfies the north-star: context restored in seconds, one owner intervention per shipped fix.
dataFlow: Step 1 — Read-only: GUI queries the CORE-owned store (workflow domain tables) for WorkflowDefinition rows + latest WorkflowRun summary per definition (status, cost aggregated from S6a call logs). No daemon involvement; nothing written.

Step 2 — CREATE WorkflowDefinition{id, project_id, name, status: draft, version: 1, canvas_layout} in the core store, written by the GUI via a core command (workflow domain is S3+ data → core-owned SQLite per the Data-layer charter; the daemon's bpa.db is never touched for this). Autosave keeps the draft row updated as he edits.

Step 3 — CREATE Trigger{id, definition_id, kind: schedule, cron: '0 3 * * *', tz, concurrency: skip, enabled: false} in the core store, child of the draft definition. NOT yet registered with the scheduler — registration happens only on enable. The 'next run' preview is computed in-memory by the core scheduler service from the cron expression.

Step 4 — CREATE Step{id, definition_id, order: 1, name: 'Ingest prod error logs', output_schema: artifact/error-log-bundle} + ToolBinding{step_id, kind: terminal, command_template_id, params} in the core store. The Terminals tab of the picker is populated from project-level command templates (core store); at RUN time this binding will make the engine spawn a PTY session via the Hop-B socket (daemon-owned), but at EDIT time nothing touches the daemon. Edge Trigger→Step1 stored as an Edge row.

Step 5 — CREATE Step 2 + ToolBinding{kind: agent, agent_role_id: research, retrieval_sources: [workspace, study_folder_artifact, project_db_ro, graph, lib_docs], allowed_mcp_tools: [prowl.prowl_analyze]} in the core store. The MCP tool list is read from the core MCP-client registry (connected servers + discovered tool catalogs, cached in the core store); prowl's stable session_id lives in project MCP settings and is referenced, not copied.

Step 10 — UPDATE WorkflowDefinition v1: validation runs in the core engine (schema-chip matching = static check of each Edge's output_schema vs input_schema; gate coverage check; binding completeness). On Save the definition + steps + bindings + edges are committed in ONE core-store transaction and the definition status flips draft→saved(disabled). Cost estimate computed from S6a pricing tables (core).

Step 11 — UPDATE Trigger.enabled=true and WorkflowDefinition.status=enabled (core store); the core SCHEDULER (a workflow-engine service in the core process) registers the cron entry in its in-memory wheel and persists next_fire_at on the Trigger row so a core restart re-hydrates schedules from the store. Home-screen card subscribes to core-store change events.

Step 12 — 'Run now': the engine CREATEs WorkflowRun{id, definition_id, definition_version: 1, trigger_source: manual, actor: owner, state: running} and StepRun rows created lazily as each step starts. Step 1: engine (core) → Hop-B socket → daemon spawns PTY session; SESSION + scrollback live in daemon bpa.db (terminal domain), StepRun stores the session_id reference + exit status + artifact pointer; the GUI's live view and the engine are two subscribers on the same session (Pv2 multi-subscriber attach, D5). Artifact 'error-log bundle' is written to the project Study folder (workspace filesystem) and registered as an Artifact row (core store) + graph node (S4). Step 2: Research agent runs IN the core process via the S6a provider layer (every LLM call logged with cost/tokens/latency); its prowl call goes through the core MCP client (egress core-only) and the request/response is persisted on the StepRun. Step 3: PM agent INSERTs Kanban cards (core store). Step 4: engine CREATEs 3 child WorkflowRuns (parent_run_id set) executing the Dev-workflow definition; child runs drive terminal workers (claude-code etc.) as daemon PTYs via S6d adapters.

Step 13 — Gate: engine sets StepRun(deploy).state=waiting_approval and CREATEs an Escalation/Approval row (S6c inbox table, core store) carrying batched context (diff refs, test results, error signatures). Owner's Approve UPDATEs the Approval row (decision, actor, timestamp → immutable audit log) which the engine observes and resumes: daemon PTY spawned for deploy (scrollback in bpa.db), then Verify agent (core) polls logs/health via its bound tools, writes its verdict to StepRun(verify), and the engine finalizes WorkflowRun.state=succeeded, aggregating duration + total cost onto the run row. Home feed updates via store events.

Step 14 — Edit: opening 'Edit' CREATEs WorkflowDefinition v2 as a copy-on-write draft (immutable v1 rows stay; runs reference definition_version). New Step 'Notify Slack' + ToolBinding{kind: mcp_tool, server: slack, tool: send_message, params_template} rows attach to v2. Connecting Slack MCP writes a McpServer row (endpoint, auth ref in Keychain, discovered tool catalog) into the core MCP registry — an app-level entity reusable by any workflow/agent.

Step 15 — Publish: core-store transaction flips v2 draft→enabled and marks v1 superseded; the scheduler entry is re-pointed at v2 (same Trigger, definition_version bumped). Pinning rule enforced by the engine: WorkflowRun.definition_version is immutable, so in-flight v1 runs finish on v1's frozen rows. Version history = the retained immutable definition rows.

Step 16 — History: GUI queries core store for WorkflowRun + StepRun trees; terminal-step replay pulls scrollback from the daemon's bpa.db by stored session_id (rehydrated as inactive sessions per the survival table); agent-step replay pulls LLM traces/costs from the S6a call log (feeds S7 dashboards); MCP-step replay pulls persisted request/response payloads; artifacts resolve via Artifact rows to study-folder files + S4 graph nodes; the approval record reads from the immutable S6c audit table. Nothing is recomputed — the whole run is replayable from stored state.

uxRaw.scenario: "A prod-error self-healing run executes (mostly autonomous)". It is 03:00; the 24h recurring workflow "Prod self-heal" fires for Project X while the owner sleeps and the GUI panel is closed. The run is hosted by a headless orchestrator process (a launchd sibling of bpa-sessiond, per the SRE-audit recommendation) so it needs no open app. It ingests production logs, dedups them into ErrorGroups, triages the worthy ones into the Study Folder, researches each (code + logs + DB + project docs + library docs via MCP), spawns fix tasks into the dev workflow (app-native specialist agent driving a claude-code terminal worker, TDD), auto-deploys under policy, verifies the fix against live error rates, and compiles a morning digest. The owner is pulled in exactly once: one low-confidence root cause parks as an escalation in the Hot Questions inbox, which he answers with a single click at 08:30. A failure branch (stuck worker / failed verify) auto-rolls-back and sends the ONE sanctioned push notification. Target state per Vision v2 — several capabilities described here do not exist yet and this scenario defines the goal.
userJourney: STEP 0 (days earlier, precondition): In Project X's Workflow tab the owner had opened the workflow editor (workflow-as-data), enabled the built-in 'Prod self-heal' recurring workflow, connected error sources (Sentry token, DigitalOcean app), and set policy knobs: auto-deploy allowed for low-risk diffs, run budget $5, quiet hours 23:00–08:00. The workflow card now shows 'next run 03:00'. Tonight he does nothing.

STEP 1 (03:00 — trigger fires): Owner is asleep, panel closed, phone silent (quiet-hours policy: notify only on high-severity escalation). Had the panel been open, the home-screen Live Agent Feed would show a new run chip appear on the Project X row: 'Self-heal · running · step 1/8 · started 03:00'.

STEP 2 (03:01 — log ingestion): Nothing owner-facing at night. In the Activity/Monitoring view the 'Ingest logs' step chip would show live counters: '12,431 records pulled (Sentry, DO app logs) · 9 error groups touched · 3 NEW since v1.4.2'.

STEP 3 (03:04 — triage into Study Folder): The Study Folder queue for Project X (a ranked list view, one row per error group) gains 3 new items, e.g. 'TypeError: null user in checkout session refresh — 214 events, new since deploy v1.4.2 — priority P1', each with status 'queued'; 6 low-signal groups appear in the collapsed 'ignored (with reason)' section.

STEP 4 (03:05–03:25 — research): Each StudyItem row flips to 'researching' with a streaming activity note ('reading stack trace → git blame src/session.ts → project docs → zod changelog via docs MCP'). Opening a StudyItem shows the growing Research artifact: findings, root-cause hypothesis, proposed fix, confidence score, source links.

STEP 5 (03:26 — fix tasks created): Project X Kanban gains 2 new cards in 'todo', tagged 'self-heal', each linked back to its StudyItem/ErrorGroup ('Fix: guard null user on session refresh · AC: regression test on stack fingerprint'). The 3rd StudyItem shows 'parked — needs your decision' (confidence below threshold) and a badge appears on the Hot Questions inbox.

STEP 6 (03:27–04:10 — build + test): Live Agent Feed shows the backend-specialist agent driving a claude-code terminal worker in an isolated worktree; the Kanban card moves todo → progress → testing on its own. Because of multi-subscriber attach (D5), the owner COULD co-view the actual live terminal from a second surface without disturbing the agent — tonight nobody watches.

STEP 7 (04:11 — pre-deploy policy gate): Nothing visible: the diff is classified low-risk (no migrations, no config/spend change, within budget), so per Project X policy the 'production deploy' approval class auto-approves. The run proceeds without waking the owner. (Counterfactual: a migration-touching diff would park here, and the whole branch would wait in the inbox until morning — durably, across orchestrator restarts.)

STEP 8 (04:12 — deploy): Activity view shows 'Deploying v1.4.3 to production (DO app) — logs streaming', with elapsed time and a manual 'Rollback' button rendered on the step chip for anyone watching.

STEP 9 (04:15–04:45 — verify): The StudyItem status shows 'verifying — watching error fingerprint for 30 min post-deploy', then flips to 'resolved — 0 recurrences'. The Kanban cards slide to 'done'. The second fix repeats steps 6–9 and also verifies clean.
STEP 10 (04:50 — run completes): No ping. The run ends 'succeeded, 1 escalation pending'; a digest entry is queued for the morning summary instead of a notification (quiet hours).

STEP 11 (08:30 — morning open, the <30s context promise): Owner opens the panel. The home screen answers immediately: Project X tile reads 'Self-heal ran 03:00 · 2 fixes shipped (v1.4.3) · error rate −78% · $2.10 · 1 needs you'; the Hot Questions inbox badge shows 1; other projects' tiles show their own overnight deltas. He has full cross-project context without opening a single terminal.

STEP 12 (08:31 — reviews the run): He clicks the tile → run timeline in the Activity view: every step with duration, acting agent, cost; replayable terminal transcript of the claude-code worker; the diff; deploy logs; a before/after error-rate chart from verification. He skims it in ~90 seconds and trusts it because nothing is faked (honest-state tenet).

STEP 13 (08:33 — answers the one escalation): He opens Hot Questions: 'payment webhook 500 — two plausible root causes; choose A (retry queue) or B (idempotency key)?' with the Research artifact inlined. He picks A, types one line of guidance, hits Approve. That is his single intervention per shipped task (north-star metric b). The parked branch visibly resumes in the Live Agent Feed within seconds.

STEP 14 (08:35 — optional steering, same screen): Still on the home screen he quick-captures an idea into Project X's backlog ('add webhook alerting') and nudges the self-heal policy (raises the auto-deploy risk threshold one notch). Two minutes total; he closes the laptop and the resumed fix branch keeps running headless.

STEP 15 (failure branch — the only 3am wake-up): IF the worker had wedged, the deploy failed, or verification showed a regression: the system auto-rolls-back to v1.4.2, marks the run failed-safe, and sends exactly ONE high-severity push: 'Self-heal on X rolled back v1.4.3 — prod stable, details in inbox'. No log walls, no terminal tabs to check; everything else waits batched for morning.
dataFlow: STEP 0: WorkflowDefinition (versioned steps, cron trigger '24h @03:00', per-step tool bindings, policy knobs) + ScheduleDefinition + ErrorSourceRegistry entries (Sentry DSN/API, DO app id; credentials in Keychain per BL-20) persisted in the CORE-OWNED domain store — served by the headless orchestrator process ('bpa-orchd', launchd sibling of bpa-sessiond) so it is readable at 3am with the GUI dead. Daemon charter untouched: bpa-sessiond still owns terminal-domain state only.

STEP 1: The scheduler inside bpa-orchd evaluates ScheduleDefinition (missed-run catch-up + overlap control: refuse to start run N+1 while N is live), creates WorkflowRun{project:X, status:running} and pending StepRun rows in the domain store, and appends a run-started event to the audit log. Actor: workflow scheduler (headless orchestrator).

STEP 2: The ingestion step (workflow step executing connectors) pulls from each source in ErrorSourceRegistry — Sentry via its MCP connector, hosting logs via the DigitalOcean MCP (apps-get-logs), optional file tails. Each record is normalized into LogRecord rows (telemetry tables in the core domain store); a dedup fingerprint (stack signature + release) CREATES new or UPDATES existing ErrorGroup entities (count, first/last_seen, sample stack, release, status). Actors: workflow step in orchestrator + MCP tools.

STEP 3: The app-native Triage agent (LLM call through the S6a provider layer, running in the orchestrator's agent runtime) scores each new/regressed ErrorGroup against triage policy (frequency, novelty, user impact, recency-vs-release). For each accepted group it CREATES StudyItem{errorGroupId, priority, status:queued} in the domain store; rejected groups get ErrorGroup.status:ignored with a stored reason. Per-call cost/tokens captured from the first call (S6a).

STEP 4: The app-native Research agent, per StudyItem: pulls the project's knowledge-graph subgraph via the S4 agent-retrieval API, reads the repo through the workspace layer, queries the project DB/log stores read-only, fetches library docs via a docs MCP, and (when external intelligence is needed) calls the prowl MCP with the project's cached stable session_id. Output: a Research artifact {findings, root-cause hypothesis, fix approach, confidence, evidence links} stored as a durable, linkable object AND inserted as a knowledge-graph node linked to the ErrorGroup; StudyItem.status:researched. Actors: app-native agent + MCP tools (prowl, docs) + core store.

STEP 5: The PM agent converts each Research with confidence ≥ policy threshold into a FixTask (spec snippet, acceptance criteria incl. regression test on the error fingerprint, TDD notes) in the core store, plus an S5 Kanban card; graph links FixTask↔StudyItem↔ErrorGroup↔Research are written. The low-confidence StudyItem instead CREATES Escalation{type:decision, options:[A,B], severity:normal, batched:true} in the escalation store (S6c) and durably SUSPENDS that branch's StepRun (status:waiting_approval). Actor: PM agent in orchestrator.

STEP 6: The engineering-specialist agent (app-native, orchestrator runtime) creates an isolated worktree, then spawns a claude-code worker via the Hop-B socket to bpa-sessiond (command+argv spawn, no shell wrapping); the S6d worker adapter owns liveness/stuck detection (waiting_for_input is blind to raw-mode TUIs). Every command lands in the daemon's command_events table with OSC-133 exit codes; scrollback persists for morning replay. Test-gate results are recorded on the StepRun; the commit lands on a fix branch; FixTask.status and Kanban card position update in the core store and stream to any attached GUI. Actors: app-native agent + terminal worker + daemon.

STEP 7: The S6c policy engine evaluates approval class 'production deploy' against Project X's policy knobs (risk classifier over the diff, budget remaining on the WorkflowRun, blast-radius rules). Auto-approve path: a PolicyDecision record with machine rationale is appended to the audit log — no entity waits. Gated path (counterfactual): StepRun suspends durably, Escalation created, WorkflowRun survives orchestrator restarts while parked. Actor: policy engine (orchestrator).

STEP 8: The deploy step executes Project X's DeployDefinition (per-project config: pipeline command or provider MCP call, environment, health check, rollback recipe). Execution runs in an audited PTY session (command_events) or via the DigitalOcean MCP (apps-update → apps-get-deployment-status polling). A Deploy entity {workflowRunId, fixTaskIds, version:v1.4.3, status:running→succeeded, logsRef, rollbackPlan} is created and updated in the core store. Actors: workflow step + terminal/MCP + daemon audit.

STEP 9: The verification step re-polls the SAME error sources, scoped to each ErrorGroup fingerprint, over the configured post-deploy window (30 min). It writes VerifyResult{deployId, errorGroupId, window, recurrences:0, verdict:fixed}. On verdict:fixed → ErrorGroup.status:resolved, StudyItem.status:done, FixTask + Kanban card → done, graph edge 'resolved-by → Deploy v1.4.3' written. (On verdict:not-fixed → jump to STEP 15's rollback flow.) Actors: workflow step + MCP connectors + core store.

STEP 10: WorkflowRun.status:succeeded_with_escalations(1); the orchestrator's digest builder aggregates the run into a per-project DigestEntry (fixes shipped, error-rate delta, $ cost from S6a per-call capture rolled up per run, escalations outstanding). Notification policy evaluates quiet hours → suppresses push, marks the digest for morning batch. Actor: orchestrator scheduler/digest builder.

STEP 11: Pure READ path: the GUI launches, attaches to bpa-orchd (domain store) and bpa-sessiond (terminal domain), hydrates home-screen tiles from WorkflowRun + DigestEntry + Escalation + Kanban aggregates. The only write: a time-to-context metric sample (north-star a) into S7 stats. Actors: GUI core process reading both stores.

STEP 12: READ path across StepRun rows, daemon command_events + scrollback records (transcript replay), LLM trace/cost records (S6a→S7), the Deploy entity's logsRef, and VerifyResult series rendered as the before/after chart. No writes except a 'run reviewed' audit marker. Actors: GUI + daemon replay.

STEP 13: Escalation.status:answered{choice:A, note} written to the core store with the owner's identity + timestamp in the audit log (the ONE human touch, feeding north-star metric b). bpa-orchd observes the answer, RESUMES the suspended StepRun: the StudyItem re-enters the pipeline at STEP 5 with the decision attached as agent context; a continuation WorkflowRun (or resumed branch) proceeds through steps 6–9 headless. Actors: owner (single write) + orchestrator resume logic.

STEP 14: Idea entity {text, project:X, status:captured} created in the core store (idea lifecycle: captured→researched→specced→in-dev→shipped); WorkflowDefinition gets a new VERSION with the changed policy knob (workflow-as-data is append-only versioned; the 03:00 scheduler binds to latest version at trigger time); both changes audited. Actors: GUI → core store; scheduler picks up next run.

STEP 15 (failure branch): S6d stuck-detection or VerifyResult{verdict:regression} triggers the rollback recipe from Deploy.rollbackPlan → a new Deploy entity {type:rollback, target:v1.4.2, status:succeeded} executed in an audited session; a post-rollback VerifyResult confirms prod stable; WorkflowRun.status:failed_safe (never an unknown prod state — honest degradation); Escalation{severity:high} created; the notification policy overrides quiet hours for severity:high and emits exactly one push. All artifacts (transcripts, logs, verify series) remain linked for the morning post-mortem. Actors: worker adapter / verify step → rollback step → notification service (all in orchestrator).

openQuestions: Store topology: the Data-layer charter says S3+ domain data lives in a 'core-owned store', but at 3am the GUI core is dead — does bpa-orchd become the store's owner/server (GUI attaches as a client, symmetric to bpa-sessiond), or do orchestrator and GUI share one SQLite file with a locking discipline? This must be decided before S3/S6b lock 'agents run in the core process'.

Does the daemon charter or S6b contract need a formal amendment to name the orchestrator as a third process, and what is ITS survival/upgrade story (drain semantics for in-flight WorkflowRuns during orchestrator upgrade)?

Escalation reach at 3am: the panel is a macOS desktop app — what is the actual push channel and answer surface for the severity-high notification (mobile web view of the inbox? notification with deep link that waits for morning? Telegram/email fallback)? Can the owner ANSWER remotely or only be informed?

Verification semantics: is a 30-min zero-recurrence window per ErrorGroup fingerprint sufficient verdict for low-traffic projects (may need traffic-aware or statistical windows), and who defines the per-project window?

Auto-deploy risk classifier: what concretely makes a diff 'low-risk' (no migrations, no dependency bumps, LOC cap, path allowlists?) and is the classifier itself an LLM call (needs its own audit + failure posture) or deterministic rules?

Rollback contract: DeployDefinition must include a TESTED rollback recipe — is a self-heal workflow allowed to run at all for projects whose deploy config lacks one (proposed: refuse + escalate at enable-time, not at 3am)?

Credentials for production sources (Sentry, hosting, DB read-only): Keychain is per-user and unlocked-session-bound — can the headless orchestrator read Keychain items at 3am with the screen locked, or does this need a different secret store?

Concurrency and blast-radius limits: how many parallel fix branches / terminal workers per run and per machine at 3am (the owner's Mac is also the build host); does the run budget cap LLM spend only or also CI/deploy actions?

Ordering vs the roadmap: this scenario needs S3 (data model), S4 (graph, hard-blocks S6), S6a–S6d, plus the new ingestion/scheduler/deploy slices — where do the new slices land (reshaped S8 vs new S9a/S9b) and what is the minimal spine for a first end-to-end self-heal run?

dataFlow: 1. READ-ONLY FAN-IN. GUI (React/Zustand in the Tauri webview) queries the CORE-owned store (S3+ domain SQLite, per Data-layer charter) for Project, Goal, Task, BugTask, Priority rows and the workflow engine's WorkflowDefinition + latest WorkflowRun state per project; Metrics snapshots come from the S7 telemetry store (core) with S8 external series cached alongside. Live agent presence is pushed by the app-native agent runtime (core process) as Tauri events; terminal-session liveness comes from the DAEMON over the Hop-B socket (session list + state pushes, daemon-owned bpa.db). Single aggregate read-model query per project card — no writes yet.

2. DELTA READ-MODEL + ONE WRITE. Core store keeps an append-only project event log (task moved, run completed, bug filed — written by agents and the workflow engine as they act). The delta strip is a query: events since OwnerPresence.last_seen_at. On open, OwnerPresence.last_seen_at is updated (core store write) so tomorrow's delta is scoped correctly.

3. BACKGROUND HISTORY (already happened, now displayed). At 03:00 the workflow SCHEDULER (core, cron-like, part of the workflow engine) instantiated a WorkflowRun of the 'prod-error-analysis' WorkflowDefinition: step1 log-ingestion pulled prod error logs into the study folder (ErrorCluster records, core store); step2 an app-native research agent ran over code/logs/DB/docs using the S4 graph retrieval API, writing ResearchArtifact rows linked into the knowledge graph; step3 created 3 BugTask rows (core store) with Priority defaults; step4 spawned terminal workers (daemon PTYs via S6d adapters) that implemented fixes; step5 (deploy) hit a P1 policy gate → Escalation record created (core store, S6c), WorkflowRun.state = waiting_approval. The GUI click is pure navigation; it reads the project-detail aggregate.

4. AGGREGATE READ + LIVE SUBSCRIPTIONS. Reads per project: Goals, Tasks, BugTasks, Priority ranks, WorkflowDefinition (steps as data) + active/most-recent WorkflowRun with per-step status, Metrics series, agent-runtime status. The webview subscribes to core event pushes for this project; core in turn holds a Hop-B subscription to the daemon for terminal state. Everything rendered is store-truth — no synthetic status (honest-state tenet).

5. PRIORITY WRITE → AGENT RE-PLAN. GUI writes the Priority entity in the core store (fractional stack-rank recompute across plan Tasks and BugTasks), appends a priority-changed event to the project event log. The app-native PM agent (core runtime) subscribes to priority events; its next queue-pull respects the new order and may reassign the in-flight specialist. No daemon involvement — purely core-store + agent runtime.

6. GOAL WRITE → GRAPH → CEO. Goal row updated in the core store; the linked knowledge-graph node (S4, UUID identity) is updated in the same transaction and the goal-changed event appended. The CEO agent's next decision cycle calls the S4 agent-retrieval API (goal subgraph <100 ms) and cites the new goal in its decision record (audit log).

7. INBOX READ + EVIDENCE JOIN. Reads Escalation records (core store) joined to their WorkflowRun, Tasks/BugTasks, and audit-log entries; cost figures come from S6a per-call cost capture. Evidence terminal transcripts resolve through core → daemon Hop-B ReadOutput{since_seq} against daemon-owned scrollback. All reads.

8. APPROVAL WRITE → RUN RESUME → DEPLOY EXECUTION. Escalation.state → approved (core store) with an audit entry (actor=owner, timestamp, evidence hash). The workflow engine observes the approval event and resumes the WorkflowRun: the deploy step executes via a terminal worker — core asks the daemon (Hop-B create/write-stdin) to run the deploy in a PTY, the S6d worker adapter supervises liveness. Step status events stream daemon → core → webview. On success: WorkflowRun → completed, the 3 BugTasks → done (kanban S5 cards move via agent-driven writes), a deploy event lands in S7 Metrics, and the inline decision answer ('Stripe not Paddle') is written back as an Escalation resolution the waiting PM agent consumes and forwards to its worker.

9. MULTI-SUBSCRIBER ATTACH (protocol v2, D5). The GUI attaches as a SECOND subscriber to the deploy session over Hop-B wire-level multi-subscriber attach, receiving its own Replay; the agent's adapter keeps its subscription. Read-only for the owner (policy: stdin writes from GUI to agent-owned sessions gated). No domain writes; scrollback stays daemon-owned.

10. METRICS READ → WORKFLOW INSTANTIATION. Metrics tab reads S7 telemetry + S8 external analytics (each row carries provenance: source, fetched_at). The button creates a WorkflowRun of the 'sprint-planning' WorkflowDefinition (workflow-as-data, core store): step1 CEO agent (app-native, core, LLM calls through S6a provider layer with cost capture) reads goals + S4 graph + Metrics snapshot (snapshot ID frozen into the run for reproducibility); step2 PM agent gap-analysis writes proposed Task rows (state=proposed) each linked to the motivating metric snapshot; step3 policy gate creates a 'sprint approval' Escalation.

11. PROPOSAL EDIT + PROMOTE. Owner's delete removes one proposed Task (soft-delete with audit); reorder writes Priority ranks. Approval flips the Escalation → approved; the workflow engine promotes Tasks proposed → backlog/todo (kanban S5), the sprint is recorded as a Sprint entity referencing the metric snapshot. Specialist agents begin pulling tasks; each spawn is a daemon PTY session created over Hop-B, visible as agent-presence events back on the dashboard.

12. MCPSERVERCONFIG CREATE + KEYCHAIN. MCPServerConfig record created in the CORE store: {name:'oxdev', server:'prowl.chat', transport/url, scope:project(shopmind), status:configuring}. The API key goes into the macOS Keychain (BL-20 pattern); the store holds only a keychain reference — never the secret. All egress is core-only (locked decision).

13. MCP CLIENT HANDSHAKE + POLICY ROWS. The core MCP client subsystem connects, runs the MCP initialize handshake, calls tools/list; the tool catalog is cached onto MCPServerConfig.tools (names, schemas, fetched_at). Per-tool ToolPolicy rows are written (auto-allowed / gated / spend-cap in $) — these are enforced by the same S6c trust layer agents already run under. Per prowl's session semantics a stable session_id is generated and persisted on the config so report cache / circuit-breaker state stay scoped. A health-check result (status, latency) is stored and re-checked on a schedule by the workflow scheduler.

14. IDEA PIPELINE: idea → research(MCP) → task → subtasks. Idea entity created (core store, state=captured, project=shopmind). Because 'research first' is set, the workflow engine instantiates the idea-research WorkflowRun: its research step invokes prowl_analyze THROUGH the core MCP client (ToolPolicy checked: auto-allowed, $10 cap; cost logged like any S6a call) using the pinned session_id; the returned report is stored as a ResearchArtifact (durable, linkable) and linked into the S4 knowledge graph; Idea.state → researched; the PM agent then forms a Task decomposed into subtasks (rows in core store) entering the standard brainstorm→spec→plan pipeline. Idea card state transitions stream to the GUI as events.

15. SURVIVAL + UNATTENDED PROGRESS. On GUI close: daemon-owned PTY sessions KEEP RUNNING (session-survival truth table); the agent runtime checkpoints run state to the core store (S6b: runs resumable after restart). TARGET behavior for 'hours unattended': a headless core/agent-host survives GUI close so app-native agents keep orchestrating — anything policy-gated accumulates as Escalation records; a scheduler-driven summary step batches them into a morning-summary notification (push/email). On next open, step 1's read-model replays exactly what happened — closing the loop on 'the owner never polls'.

report.executiveSummary: The docs are excellent at what they cover — a hardened terminal engine, a disciplined protocol-evolution story, a principled data charter, and a credible agent-org spine — but they cover the ORIGINAL vision, not v2. Measured against "take any idea to a working project and orchestrate vibecoding," the current overview is missing all five of v2's load-bearing subsystems: the workflow engine (workflow-as-data), the MCP client, the Idea entity/pipeline, production telemetry ingestion, and the cross-project control panel; grep confirms zero hits for workflow/scheduler/MCP/idea/ingest across every spec. Worse than absence, two locked decisions actively contradict v2: overview §4 hardcodes the CEO→PM→eng loop as compiled code rather than an editable definition, and the process topology (agents in the GUI process, daemon charter-barred from domain data) makes unattended 24h execution impossible as architected. The good news is that roughly half of v2 is already built or designed under other names — Hop-B + multi-subscriber attach + command_events is the workflow engine's terminal substrate, S6c's inbox IS the hot-questions queue, S6a's cost capture and BL-20's Keychain rule generalize to MCP verbatim — so the correction is mostly re-mapping and re-ordering, not rebuilding. Four structural moves close the gap. First, decide the unattended-execution host NOW (recommended: a headless bpa-orchd launchd sibling owning the app-domain store, GUI as client) — this single ADR gates the scheduler, the 24h loop, and physically determines where every v2 entity lives, so it must precede the S3 store decision. Second, insert the workflow engine (SW1) between S6a and S6b and rewrite §4 so the agent pipeline is the DEFAULT WorkflowDefinition executed by the engine — otherwise S6b/S6c bake the pipeline into code and v2's editability costs a rewrite. Third, land the entity map now: expand S3 to Projects+Goals+Ideas+Tasks/Subtasks, update the charter with all ~9 v2 entity families, and add the S-MCP and S9a-telemetry slices so the mission's entry point (ideas) and the flagship loop's input (prod errors) have data models before schemas lock. Fourth, re-cut the order so the first user-visible v2 capability — idea → prowl research → task — ships on S3+S-MCP alone, before the agent org, de-risking the Tool Registry contract early. With those moves plus a §1 mission rewrite and the SH mission-control slice, every v2 capability has an owned home and the existing strengths carry most of the weight.
report.missionAlignment: Honestly: the overview today serves the original "director of AI development teams" mission well and the v2 mission poorly. §1 frames the product as goal-setting over an agent org — accurate but silent on ideas as the entry point, the idea→research→task→design→dev pipeline, workflow-as-data, MCP extensibility, and the always-on cross-project panel; a zero-context implementer reading it would build an agent-orchestration shell, not an idea-to-project machine (V30 is the root cause of every missing slice). "Orchestrate vibecoding" fares slightly better because the terminal/worker/approval substrate is genuinely strong, but "any idea → working project" has literally no data model, no research vehicle, and no delivery step. The single biggest structural gap is the absence of the workflow engine combined with its host-process problem (V1+V2): v2's central claim — the development workflow is DATA the owner edits, running unattended on schedules — has no slice, no storage home, and no process that survives window-close. Everything else (ideas, MCP, telemetry, metrics→sprint, the panel) either hangs off that engine or feeds it; until SW1 and the host ADR exist, v2's recurring capabilities are not just unbuilt but undesignable, because no other slice can even declare a dependency on them.

revisedRoadmap.realizesVision: 'The owner can change the flow and keep it flexible' — editing workflows becomes a sanctioned human step (§5).

revisedRoadmap.slice: S6d / S6e (largely unchanged)
revisedRoadmap.purpose: External worker adapters (liveness/stuck detection) as step workers; custom-agent authoring where 'tools' = Tool Registry ids and custom agents/chains are definitions on the same substrate.
revisedRoadmap.realizesVision: Custom chains built from the same tools; heterogeneous workers inside workflows.

revisedRoadmap.slice: S9a: Project telemetry ingestion — prod errors + study folder (NEW)
revisedRoadmap.purpose: Per-project LogSourceConfig registry (error-tracker APIs, hosting log pulls, file tails, MCP-backed connectors; credentials in Keychain), pull/tail transports with retries + honest degradation, normalized ErrorEvent with fingerprint dedup (count, first/last_seen, bounded samples), StudyItem triage queue with its own lifecycle (new→under-research→task-created→fix-deployed→verified/recurred), raw payloads on the filesystem ('study folder') with DB index rows, telemetry data class retention/redaction/purge. Research source connectors (read-only prod-DB DSN, docs) with audit. Shares one connector substrate with S8.
revisedRoadmap.realizesVision: The 24h self-healing loop's INPUT: 'every 24h analyze the project's production error logs'; the loop's memory.

revisedRoadmap.slice: S9b: Delivery/deploy step + verification (NEW, thin)
revisedRoadmap.purpose: Per-project deploy config (command/target from S3 ops section), execution via terminal workers (command_events = the run record; not a CD system), gating on the EXISTING 'production deploy' class, DeployRecord history with rollback recipe, and verification as a first-class step type (watch ingested events for the fixed fingerprint over a window; recurrence reopens the StudyItem and escalates; success closes with evidence). The composed 'prod self-heal' default WorkflowDefinition ships here as SW1+SW2+S9a+S9b's joint DoD.
revisedRoadmap.realizesVision: 'Fix tasks get deployed' and 'the project watches its own production errors and fixes them' — the loop actually closes, honestly.

revisedRoadmap.slice: S7 (extended): Observability incl. workflow-run health
revisedRoadmap.purpose: Existing agent/LLM scope plus: scheduled-run health (last success, consecutive failures, missed runs), per-workflow-run cost rollup over Llm/McpCallRecords, 'recurring action failed/stopped' alert into the inbox.
revisedRoadmap.realizesVision: v2 law #1 for unattended loops: a silently dead 24h loop is worse than none; spend attributable per run.

revisedRoadmap.slice: S8 (re-scoped, no longer '(future)'): Metrics ingestion + metrics→sprint workflow
revisedRoadmap.purpose: Per-project external metrics/analytics via the S9a connector substrate; MetricPoint timeseries (append-only, retention/downsample) with S6a/MCP call records as the first internal sources; Sprint entity (window, planned tasks, planning-run provenance); metric events + thresholds trigger the sprint-planning WorkflowDefinition. DoD: a metric-triggered run completes end-to-end producing a prioritized task set (keeps the existing provenance DoD).
revisedRoadmap.dependsOn: S3 (data), SW1/SW2 (workflow+trigger), S9a (connectors); S7 only for dashboards
revisedRoadmap.realizesVision: 'The system observes metrics and plans the sprint' — a recurring workflow co-equal with the error loop.

revisedRoadmap.slice: SH: Mission-control home / cross-project control panel (NEW, capstone)
revisedRoadmap.purpose: Six lanes per project (goals, plan tasks, bug-fix tasks, cross-project prioritization, delivery/workflow state, monitoring), 'what moved since last look' delta strips, live agent feed on Pv2 multi-subscriber attach, idea quick-capture, vector steering (goals), hot-questions widget = the S6c inbox, agent-org settings entry, and the cross-project prioritization model (a ranking spanning ideas/tasks — currently absent everywhere). DoD: cold open answers where-is-every-project + what-needs-me in <30 s.
revisedRoadmap.dependsOn: S6c, S7, SW1 run state, S-IDEA, S9a/S9b lanes
revisedRoadmap.realizesVision: 'The panel is the single place the owner directs all projects from'; north-star (a) time-to-context <30 s across 5–6 projects.

correctionPlan.connects: Umbrella for every slice this plan adds; pairs with the SH slice adopting metric (a) as its DoD.

correctionPlan.why: Three locked decisions jointly foreclose unattended execution today (agents in the GUI process, S3+ data core-owned, daemon charter-barred). This ADR gates SW2, the 24h loop, AND physically determines where every v2 entity lives — so it must precede the S3 store-engine decision, not wait for S6.
correctionPlan.fromTo: from agents 'in the core process' + survival row 'Agent runs (S6+) — undefined until S6b' + no host for schedules → to a named host decision with a filled survival row and drain/upgrade story.
correctionPlan.connects: Gates SW1/SW2 hosting and S3's physical store home; consumes the launchd/runbook/BL-19/D4 patterns; the #1 open question for the owner.

correctionPlan.change: Add two one-line locks to §2: (1) 'every S2+ data model, store, and event stream is multi-project from day one; UI panels are project-scoped VIEWS over multi-project state'; (2) 'LLM providers (model calls — S6a) and MCP tool providers (tool calls — S-MCP) are distinct subsystems joined only at the Tool Registry.'
correctionPlan.why: Prevents the two cheapest-to-prevent rewrites: mission control becoming a store/event rework instead of a composition, and the MCP client getting entangled with model routing/fallback semantics that don't apply to tool servers.
correctionPlan.fromTo: from single-project-phrased S2–S5 DoDs and one undifferentiated 'provider' concept → to explicit multi-project + two-axes locks all slices cite.
correctionPlan.connects: Enables SH to be a composition; keeps S-MCP out of S6a's dependency chain (and vice versa).

correctionPlan.change: Update the Data-layer charter with the full v2 entity map and owning slices: DAEMON bpa.db unchanged (sessions, scrollback, terminal-workspaces, command_events). APP-DOMAIN store (engine locked in the S3 spec, host per ADR-HOST): S3 → Project, Goal, Idea, ResearchArtifact(index), Task, Subtask; S4 → GraphNode/Edge + entity-reference node type; S6a → LlmCallRecord; S-MCP → McpServerConfig, McpToolCatalogCache, McpSessionState, McpCallRecord; SW1/SW2 → WorkflowDefinition (versioned), WorkflowRun, StepState, Trigger/Schedule; S9a/S9b → LogSourceConfig, ErrorEvent, StudyItem, DeployRecord; S7/S8 → MetricPoint, Sprint. Rule: S3 sizes the engine against this WHOLE map (SQLite/WAL likely fine; big blobs on filesystem with DB index rows); terminal evidence stays daemon-side linked by session_id.
correctionPlan.why: Unassigned entities default into whichever process is convenient (most likely bpa.db — a direct charter violation — or ad-hoc JSON), and an engine chosen for planning-CRUD scale can be wrong for run logs, error streams, and timeseries. The charter exists precisely to stop this drift; it just needs the v2 rows.
correctionPlan.fromTo: from charter enumerating only projects/goals/kanban/graph → to the complete ~9-family entity map with owning slices and a sizing rule.
correctionPlan.connects: Umbrella for the S3/S4/S-MCP/SW/S9/S8 specs; host decided by ADR-HOST; consumed by the migration and telemetry-class amendments below.

correctionPlan.change: Add to the charter: the app-domain store ships from schema v1 with its own user_version + fail-closed, forward-only, single-transaction migrations, explicitly reusing the daemon's persistence.rs machinery as the template; WorkflowDefinition carries a format_version with an append-only evolution rule (mirror the Hop-B protocol-evolution discipline: additive fields, cross-version decode test per format change); S3 export/import doubles as the backup path.
correctionPlan.whereDoc: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-01-builderpro-platform-overview.md — Data-layer charter; locked in the future S3 and SW1 specs
correctionPlan.why: The store holding the MOST schema-volatile v2 data (user-edited workflows, ideas, metrics) currently has NO migration policy while the frozen terminal DB has a rigorous one; the first schema bump becomes improvisation and a format change silently breaks the owner's saved workflow library.
correctionPlan.fromTo: from 'export/import round-trips' as the only durability DoD → to versioned store + versioned definition format with proven, transplanted machinery.
correctionPlan.connects: Reuses Pv2 §7.1 verbatim (strength, not new design); SW1's run-pinning rule depends on definition versioning.

correctionPlan.change: Add one charter rule BEFORE BL-4 lands: cross-store references are SOFT (UUID strings, no integrity assumption); the app-domain store is the system of record for run history — on step completion the engine SNAPSHOTS the step's command_events slice, exit codes, and a bounded transcript excerpt into StepState. Annotate BL-4: daemon retention purges freely because completed-run evidence is copied out; never extend daemon retention to 'keep sessions referenced by runs'.
correctionPlan.why: BL-4 (20 exited/workspace, 30-day TTL) and Pv2 §7.2 cascade will silently destroy workflow-run evidence: a run older than 30 days would point at purged sessions — an amnesiac audit trail for a product whose run history is a feature. BL-4 is about to be built, so this is time-critical.
correctionPlan.fromTo: from two DBs with no cross-reference policy and an implied FK assumption → to soft refs + snapshot-on-completion, with the app store as system of record.
correctionPlan.connects: SW1's StepState model implements the snapshot; keeps the stores decoupled (charter discipline preserved); S7 dashboards consume the same snapshots.

correctionPlan.change: Amend the charter with a third data class — 'ingested telemetry': store home decided in the S9a spec (core-owned or dedicated store, never bpa.db), size/time-bounded retention windows, redaction posture, purge-on-project-delete; add backlog rows mirroring BL-3/BL-4 for this class.
correctionPlan.why: Ingested prod logs are potentially the largest AND most sensitive data volume (USERS' data and secrets, not the owner's) — without a class they land wherever is handy, grow unboundedly, and persist PII with no purge posture.
correctionPlan.fromTo: from two charter buckets (daemon terminal domain; S3+ core store) → to three, with retention/redaction/purge rules for telemetry.
correctionPlan.connects: S9a is the owning slice; mirrors BL-3/BL-4 patterns; interacts with the S3 store-engine sizing rule.

correctionPlan.change: Generalize the credential posture: (a) charter line — 'the MCP/tool-server registry (servers, transports, enabled tools, project scope) is core-owned S3+ domain data; the daemon never sees it'; (b) §16/BL-20 retitled and widened to 'Provider AND MCP-server AND per-project source credentials (API keys, OAuth tokens, session secrets): macOS Keychain only, never SQLite/config/logs; all integration egress is core-process-only'; (c) §5 sanctioned human steps gains 'one-time interactive OAuth authorization of an MCP server, batched via the S6c inbox'; (d) extend the no-secrets-in-logs test contract to MCP request/response logs.
correctionPlan.why: BL-20 is scoped exclusively to LLM keys; the path of least resistance during the MCP slice is a plaintext prowl key in a config row — exactly the trap A9/BL-20 already closed once. Generalizing now costs one sentence; retrofitting costs an audit.
correctionPlan.fromTo: from 'Provider API keys (BL-20): Keychain only' (LLM-only) → to one integration-credential posture covering LLM, MCP, and research-source credentials, with OAuth as a sanctioned human step.
correctionPlan.connects: S-MCP and S9a specs implement it; V24's read-only source credentials reuse it; aligns with the §16 MCP boundary below.

correctionPlan.change: Add an 'MCP boundary' subsection to §16 (posture now, details in the S-MCP spec): (1) all MCP egress core-process-only; (2) per-server data-scope declaration + consent at registration (which projects/data classes may be sent), surfaced in the S6c inbox; (3) tool results AND tool descriptions are UNTRUSTED input — same advisory-never-authoritative class as OSC data — with agent-context provenance recorded; (4) every tool invocation lands in the append-only audit log with args/result digests; (5) spend-bearing tools fall under the existing P1 spend/payment class; (6) local stdio registration requires an explicit code-execution trust ack; remote servers pin TLS. Mirror a P1 row into backlog.md.
correctionPlan.why: An MCP server is a remote code/data trust boundary the current §16 doesn't know exists: prompt injection via tool results is the canonical MCP attack against an agent holding terminal power, and the 24h loop shipping DB rows + source to a third party without consent is silent exfiltration by design — load-bearing at 3am when nobody watches.
correctionPlan.fromTo: from §16 covering paths/env/socket/OSC/logging/keys with zero external-tool-server language → to a named MCP trust boundary extending (never duplicating) the existing agent trust layer.
correctionPlan.connects: Extends the §16 trust layer per the V34 reuse rule; consent + spend approvals route to S6c; V10's trust classes map onto the approval classes; V28's sampling decision cites it.

correctionPlan.change: Add explicit generalization cross-references: §16 trust-layer subsection gains 'this layer also gates MCP tool invocations (spend-bearing/destructive tool classes)'; the S6a cost-capture bullet gains '(the same record discipline applies to MCP tool calls — McpCallRecord mirrors LlmCallRecord; S7 unifies model spend and tool spend)'. File ONE P3 backlog idea: expose the app itself as an MCP server (Hop-B capabilities as MCP tools) so external agents can drive Builder Pro.
correctionPlan.why: A zero-context S-MCP implementer would plausibly build a parallel consent dialog, a second secrets path, and its own metrics table — three duplicated subsystems and a fragmented audit trail — purely because nothing SAYS the existing pieces generalize.
correctionPlan.fromTo: from four locked pieces that fit MCP but don't say so → to explicit 'reuse, don't fork' pointers in the docs the implementer will actually read.
correctionPlan.connects: Prevents duplication across S-MCP/S6a/S6c/S7; the P3 idea connects §4's forward contract to the broader agent ecosystem.

correctionPlan.change: Reshape overview §3 (table + ASCII diagram) to the revised roadmap: add SW1 (between S6a and S6b; S6b depends on SW1), SW2, SW3, S-MCP (deps: S3 + BL-20 pattern only — NOT Pv2, NOT S6a), S-IDEA (deps: S3 + S-MCP + S4, before the agent org), S9a, S9b, SH; re-scope S8 (drop '(future)', correct deps to S3+SW1/SW2+S9a-substrate, new DoD 'metric-triggered run completes end-to-end producing a prioritized task set'); add one line each to S5 and S7 noting they consume the domain event bus rather than inventing eventing.

correctionPlan.change: Rewrite overview §4: (1) loop preamble becomes 'the CEO→PM→eng loop is the DEFAULT WorkflowDefinition — an instance of workflow-as-data executed by the engine (SW1); owners can edit, reorder, and extend it', with brainstorm→spec→plan as named reorderable steps; (2) add a 'Tool Registry (forward contract)' paragraph: Tool = {id, source built-in|MCP|chain, name, description, JSON-schema I/O, trust class read-only/spend-bearing/destructive, invoke() with typed errors + scope parameter, per-call record}; SW1 locks StepBinding with three implementations (terminal via Hop-B, app-native agent, MCP tool); S6e 'tools' = registry ids; (3) state the engine's terminal-step executor drives Hop-B directly, binds runs to session_id, consumes command_events + typed exit-wait as step-status truth, and that live tap/co-watch = additional attach subscribers — forbid parallel bespoke channels; (4) name the 'Pv2.1 additive batch' (four agent requests) as owned by SW1; (5) add '§4 step 1 gains: or from a captured Idea'.

The Tool Registry is the shared contract a contracts-first project must lock before three consumers each invent their own binding. The substrate-reuse statement converts an ownership gap into a one-paragraph fix.

correctionPlan.change: Amend the S6c row: intake sources include workflow human-approval STEPS and policy gates (spend, destructive ops, deploy, spec approvals, MCP consent) in addition to agent escalations; the inbox is the single queue across ALL projects; extend the approval-class table with per-project/per-environment policy knobs; define 'awaiting-approval' as a durable workflow-run state persisted with the run and resumed by inbox action, surviving restarts. SH surfaces it as the hot-questions widget rather than building its own.

correctionPlan.fromTo: from agent-escalation-scoped, implicitly single-project inbox → to the one generic, cross-project, durable-suspend gate for agents AND workflows.
correctionPlan.connects: V7's generic-gate framing; V8's suspend/resume; V17's deploy gating; V13's MCP consent; SH's hot-questions lane; north-star metric (b).

correctionPlan.change: Extend the S7 row's scope and DoD: workflow-run health dashboard (last success, consecutive failures, missed runs); 'recurring action failed/missed N times' alert routed to the S6c inbox; per-workflow-run cost rollup built on S6a's per-call records (and McpCallRecords). Clearly distinguish S7 (app-internal observability) from S9a (per-project PRODUCTION telemetry) in §3 so the two are never conflated.
correctionPlan.why: A silently dead 24h loop is worse than no loop — the owner believes prod is watched when it isn't; and S6a captures per-call cost but nothing rolls it up per run, so a runaway nightly loop burns budget unwatched. S7 is also easily misread as covering prod-error ingestion, which it does not.

correctionPlan.change: Write the S-MCP slice spec (next cycle, Superpowers pipeline with Context7 verification of the then-current MCP spec/SDKs): server registry + auth (Keychain/OAuth) + stdio & Streamable HTTP transports + JSON-RPC client + tool discovery with list-changed + typed invoke with retries/timeouts/honest degradation + McpCallRecord + management UI. Locks the Tool Registry/StepBinding contract (first slice that needs it, before S6b). Includes from day one: invocation scope parameter + per-(server, scope) McpSessionState persisted in the core store, restored across restarts, expired with the run (prowl's stable session_id lives here). Bounds the v1 surface: tools + auth only; resources/prompts deferred with backlog rows; sampling disabled by default — if ever enabled it routes through S6a with per-server budget caps + the P1 spend class. DoD: prowl connected, tools listed, one research tool invoked, result persisted as a durable artifact.
correctionPlan.why: Without a named slice the MCP client gets improvised mid-S6b under delivery pressure — the exact anti-pattern A8 fixed for the LLM layer — and a stateless-first Tool contract would break prowl's session semantics for every consumer once locked.
correctionPlan.fromTo: from zero MCP design surface anywhere → to a bounded, secured, session-aware MCP client spec that owns the product's shared tool abstraction.
correctionPlan.connects: Implements V3/V10/V27/V28 under the §16 MCP boundary and generalized BL-20; positioned per V29 (deps S3 only); S-IDEA is its first consumer, S6a/S6b its second.

correctionPlan.change: Write the SW1+SW2 workflow-engine spec: versioned WorkflowDefinition (format_version, copy-on-write publish, runs pin their version), step kinds (agent-turn | terminal-command | mcp-tool | human-approval | verification | sub-workflow), StepBinding with the three implementations, WorkflowRun/StepState persistence + evidence snapshot-on-completion, step executor driving Hop-B (owns the Pv2.1 batch; non-goal: parallel terminal channels), triggers cron|event|manual, persisted schedules with next_fire_at rehydration, missed-run catch-up policy, overlap control, durable awaiting-approval suspend/resume via S6c, alert-on-consecutive-failures, and the internal domain event bus (typed events, durable outbox, subscriptions from triggers/kanban/stats/home feed). Verification step type: bind (deploy run, error fingerprint, watch window); recurrence reopens the StudyItem and escalates; success closes with evidence. Ships the CEO→PM→eng 'dev pipeline' and 'idea-research' definitions as the seed library.
correctionPlan.why: This is v2's central engine and the single largest missing subsystem; specifying it before S6b hardens is the difference between the agent pipeline being an INSTANCE of the engine versus a rewrite obstacle. openQuestionsForOwner: ADR-HOST (gates everything unattended): which host for the app-domain store + scheduler + agent runtime — (a) new headless bpa-orchd launchd sibling with the GUI as client [architect's recommendation], (b) widen bpa-sessiond's charter with a separated orchestration domain, or (c) honest v0 'schedules fire only while the app runs' with catch-up-on-launch, recorded as a conscious deferral? This must be decided before the S3 spec locks the store.

Intervention budget vs gates: v2 targets ~1 intervention per shipped task, but the designed pipeline has two mandatory P1 gates (breakdown approval + spec approval) plus deploy. Which gates are hard by default, which are per-project policy (e.g. auto-proceed breakdown for small tasks, auto-deploy low-risk diffs), and what concretely defines a 'low-risk' diff (no migrations? LOC cap? path allowlist? deterministic rules vs an LLM classifier)?

3am escalation reach: the panel is a desktop app — what is the actual push channel and answer surface for a severity-high escalation when the owner is away from the Mac (macOS notification only, Telegram/email fallback, mobile web view of the inbox)? Can he ANSWER remotely or only be informed until morning? Related: can the headless process read Keychain items with the screen locked, or does unattended execution need a different secret-access story?

Roadmap re-cut sign-off: accept that the ideas+research pipeline (S-IDEA, deps S3+S-MCP+S4) ships BEFORE the agent org (S6b–S6e), and that SW1 slots between S6a and S6b delaying S6b by one slice? This trades a later agent org for earlier v2 value and no pipeline rework.

prowl session scope: one stable session_id per PROJECT (keeps report cache/context across ideas, risks cross-idea bleed in Refine calls) or per idea/research-run (clean isolation, loses cache)? Needs locking before the S-MCP spec.
MCP v1 surface: confirm tools+auth only, sampling disabled by default (a remote server spending on your OpenRouter keys), resources/prompts deferred to backlog — or do you want any of these in v1?

Self-heal enable-time prerequisites: may a project enable the self-heal workflow WITHOUT a tested rollback recipe in its deploy config (proposal: refuse + escalate at enable time, never discover it at 3am)? And does a run budget breach pause the WorkflowRun as a gated escalation or fail it?

Degradation policy for the idea pipeline: when prowl is down/unauthorized, does the pipeline offer 'skip research, form task from idea only' inline (with an honest-degradation notice recorded on the artifact chain), or block until the server recovers?

Cross-project prioritization semantics: one global stack rank per project mixing plan and bug tasks, plus a cross-project ranking at the panel level — and do owner-set ranks hard-override CEO/PM-computed priorities or act as weighted/pinned input?
strengthsToPreserve: The Data-layer charter's two-domain discipline (daemon = terminal domain ONLY; app-domain data in a core-owned store; Project⇄Workspace locked): every new v2 entity family slots in as new rows under existing governance — the plan must extend the charter, never route around it or let anything accrete into bpa.db.

Hop-B as the canonical programmatic agent API + Pv2's multi-subscriber attach + command_events with OSC-133 exit codes: the complete, tested substrate for workflow terminal steps, run evidence, live agent feed, and human/agent co-viewing — SW1/SH specs must consume it and explicitly forbid parallel bespoke channels.

The protocol-evolution policy (append-only variants, frozen preamble, version negotiation, cross-version decode tests): guarantees Pv2 never needs reopening for v2 and doubles as the template for WorkflowDefinition format versioning — the single most important de-risking decision already on the books.

S6a's 'per-call cost/token/latency capture from the first call' + BL-20's Keychain-only/egress-core-only rules: the never-backfillable metrics discipline and the secure credential path that generalize verbatim to MCP call records and MCP/server credentials — reuse the record shape and the rule, never a second capture path or secrets store.

§16's agent execution trust layer + S6c's approval classes (incl. 'production deploy'), batched inbox, and append-only audit: a generic dangerous-action interception chassis that already IS v2's hot-questions queue and the unattended loop's human gate — extend with policy knobs and durable suspend/resume, never fork a parallel gate or consent dialog.

S4's UUID node identity, cross-project links, and agent retrieval API (+ D6's hard-block of S6): the ready home for research artifacts and the provenance graph — add write/ingest and entity-reference nodes; do not invent a second knowledge store.
Pv2 §7.1's fail-closed, forward-only migration machinery (persistence.rs) and the S3 export/import DoD: proven persistence patterns to transplant into the app-domain store rather than redesign.

The survival-truth-table honest-placeholder pattern and S6b's PM decomposition loop: extend the table with workflow/schedule rows instead of overclaiming, and seed the engine's default pipeline from the PM loop + the proven Superpowers brainstorm→spec→plan process — v2's canonical first WorkflowDefinition already exists as practice.
